blockers.title: The entry gate and position sizing favour low predicted variance, which is when fees cost the most relative to the move

blockers.mechanism: Price discovery happens on the perp, and the system cannot see it. The information that does exist is sub-minute microstructure that a polled 1-min architecture cannot act on, and it is 5-70x smaller than costs. Adding it will not make 1-15 min direction trading profitable. Its value is in execution.
blockers.fix_or_test: Do not build streaming infrastructure to chase alpha. If a slower rule passes (blockers 1-2), use basis and flow only to time entries and to choose maker or taker. Decisive test: on archived aggTrades or bookDepth, compare fill at bar close with fill conditioned on flow/basis over the next N seconds, for the slower rule's trades.

blockers.fix_or_test: Run a separate cheap study: a weekly cross-sectional momentum/size long-short on the top 30 Binance perps (data.binance.vision klines and funding, 2+ years), with costs and funding. verdicts.title: The 1/5/15-minute horizons are hard-coded where the fee per trade is larger than any achievable edge
verdicts.corrected_evidence: The hurdle table reproduces exactly (hurdle.py: E|r| 4.2/3.0, 9.6/6.9, 16.4/11.6, 33.2/23.2, 62.1/47.3, 155/104 bps; p*@4 at 15m 62.2/67.2%; rho*@4 0.21/0.28 at 15m, 0.06/0.07 at 240m). Correction on 'hard-coded': in model.py the horizons are a config list (HORIZON_STEPS, model.py:58, read at :288) and RESAMPLE_MINUTES (model.py:43, implemented at :219-231) already turns [1,5,15] into 1h/5h/15h with one setting. The real hard-coding is in SRS FR-3.1 and in the research harness: research/tsfm_eval/bench/common.py:18 HORIZONS=[1,5,15], research/timestral_lig/data.py:20 and trading_nocost.py:21. So nothing in the research has ever measured h>15. Nothing in the current data shows skill at longer horizons either. Block-bootstrapped variance ratios: VR(60) 0.88 [0.76,1.02] repo, 0.98 [0.85,1.06] clean; VR(240) 0.89 [0.67,1.12] / 0.92 [0.71,1.07]. The non-overlapping lag-1 autocorrelation at 240m is +0.10 / -0.03 (SE 0.07). Caveat on rho*: the formula charges the full round trip every period. Always-in sign trading pays only on flips (about 50%), so its bar is about half as high.
verdicts.notes: The arithmetic and the mechanism are right: a fixed bps fee against moves that scale with sqrt(h) makes 1-15 min the worst place to trade. The 'restriction' is cheap to lift in model.py, and the harness needs only a parameter change. But the tension with blocker 3 is not stated. At h=240 the edge needed falls to about 53-54%. Detecting 53% with 80% power then needs about 2,180 independent outcomes, which is about 360 days of out-of-sample data per test. So longer horizons lower the cost bar but raise the data and stationarity bar about one for one. A known 1-min fact supports the direction of the claim: the 1-min tower (p*@4 = 97.5% / >100%) is worthless even at maker fees and should be dropped.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No on its own. It only moves the experiment to where a 51-54% hit rate or an IC of 0.06-0.14 would pay at 4 bps. No such skill has been measured at 60-240 min (VR CIs include 1). It is profitable only together with a skill found at h>=60 on multi-year data (blocker 3) and perp-level fees (blocker 2).

verdicts.title: The venue is Binance spot at retail fees, long-only, while the liquid BTC market and the cheaper fees are on the perp
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: dw_ccxt.py:14 ccxt.binance (spot) and :48 'BTC/USDT'; spot 10 bps per side (20 bps round trip, 15 with the BNB discount), perp 2/5 bps per side; perp/spot BTC volume 6.4-6.6x (repo) and 8.7x (clean); SHORT entries at inference.ipynb cell 5 lines 278-279, PnL at 312-313 with no fee and no borrow. The fade numbers reproduce (spot q=0.98: +3.99 bps, n=287, t 2.21 / +2.20, n=359, t 1.60). Stress test (scratchpad/verif/fade_check.py): on perp prices the fade nets -0.09 (repo) and -1.74 (clean) bps at 4 bps; with a one-bar entry delay, -0.83 / -2.20; at 10 bps (taker), -6 to -9 bps in all 12 variants. The q=0.98 choice is the best of the variants: q=0.95 gives +0.6 to +1.4 bps gross, and q=0.99 gives +4.3 bps on repo but +0.8 to +1.3 on clean. 'About break-even at 4 bps' holds for repo only.
verdicts.notes: The fee half of the blocker is right and important. It cuts the cost bar 2-5x, and no rule tested anywhere survives 20 bps. The short-selling half is overstated as a money loser. The direction head says DOWN at almost every origin because of the focal alpha bias (D3), so its short calls are noise. On spot they could not be executed, which saves fees rather than losing profit. The real defect is that the notebook backtest books those shorts on spot with no borrow cost and no fees, which is a fidelity bug (D5). Also, 4 bps assumes maker fills on both legs at the bar close. For a fade entered right after a large move, a resting limit order is filled mostly when the move continues (adverse selection). The realistic case is maker in, taker out (about 7 bps), and there the fade loses 3-5 bps per trade on both sets.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No on its own. It is a necessary condition, because every candidate rule seen so far (gross +1 to +7 bps) is dead at spot fees. But the best pre-existing rule is still at or below zero on perp at maker fees, and it loses at taker fees. It is profitable only together with a selection that raises gross profit per trade above about 7 bps (see blocker 4).

verdicts.title: Only close prices reach the model; high/low, volume, trade count and taker-buy volume are dropped
verdicts.corrected_evidence: The code facts are right: model.py:244 returns only Close; model.py:1219 has a single 'close_sequence' input; dw_ccxt.py:110 keeps 6 kline fields. The vol.py table reproduces: HAR+range against HAR is -4.4/-7.1/-9.5 points (repo) and -3.3/-4.9/-4.6 (clean) at h=5/15/60. But the stated framing is too favourable. (a) A plain Parkinson EWMA is worse than the returns EWMA by +1.0 to +10.1% QLIKE (repo) and +1.0 to +8.5% (clean), so the range helps only inside a fitted HAR. (b) Against the plain EWMA baseline, HAR+range is worse at h=1 (+0.3/+4.9%) and at h=5 on clean (+1.4%). The gain over the best simple baseline is -2.6%/+1.4% at h=5 and -5.0/-8.4% at h=15. (c) The target is the sum of squared 1-min returns, not the benchmark's y^2; it uses a single 50/50 split with no CI. Taker imbalance's next-minute IC of 0.018-0.027 is worth about 0.1 bps per trade, and it decays to -0.010..+0.005 after one bar (delay.py).
verdicts.notes: This is a real unrealized SRS item: the SRS specifies 60-min OHLCV input (SRS line 387) but the code feeds close only. It is also a cheap gain for the risk path at h>=15. It does not unblock profit, because a better variance forecast earns nothing on its own (blocker 8 has no venue). Its only money path is as a better input to the vol gate in blocker 4, and that gate already works with a crude Parkinson EWMA rank. Keeping all 12 kline fields at download costs nothing and should be done anyway.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. At most it gives a small improvement to the volatility gate in blocker 4, which already works with a crude EWMA rank. Order-flow fields add about 0.1 bps per trade at 1 min and nothing after one bar of delay.

verdicts.title: With a single spot venue the system cannot see perp basis or perp order flow, but that information decays within one minute and is far smaller than fees
verdicts.corrected_evidence: flow.py and delay.py reproduce: dbasis1 IC +0.035 (t 4.9) / +0.060 (t 12.1) at h=1; with a one-bar delay -0.006/+0.004; perp imbalance +0.025/+0.034, delayed -0.008/+0.001; top-decile gross +0.64-0.76 / +0.27-0.29 bps. Stronger than stated: out-of-sample on the clean set, the '+perp' model has R^2 -0.81% even at h=1, IC -0.018 (R^2 -4.0%) at h=15 and IC -0.030 (R^2 -5.5%) at h=60. Beyond one minute, the perp features make the forecast worse. Part of the dbasis1 'signal' is probably non-synchronous bar closes (spot's last trade in the minute falls earlier than the perp's), which no order can capture.
verdicts.notes: The critic's own conclusion (do not build streaming to chase alpha) is right. That makes this an information gap rather than a blocker to profit, so the impact should be low, not medium. The only realistic use is execution timing or the maker/taker choice for a slower rule that already works, and no such rule exists yet.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. The gross effect is 0.3-0.8 bps per trade against 4-20 bps of costs, it vanishes with a one-bar delay, and it turns negative out of sample at 15-60 min. It is possibly a small execution saving only after a slower rule passes on its own.

A 25-30 bps 4-leg round trip at 0.30-0.38 bps per 8h needs 66-100 funding periods (about 22-33 days) just to break even. But the cited evidence (Liu & Tsyvinski 2021; Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022) comes from 2014-2020 samples over many coins, including small, illiquid ones. How these factors performed after costs and after publication on the top-30 Binance perps in 2024-2026 is unknown, and crowding is plausible. This is a different system, not a fix that unblocks neural_trade. It is the one route with published, cost-aware evidence, so a cheap pre-registered study is reasonable, but it should be treated as a new project.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: Unknown, and not for neural_trade as built. A weekly cross-sectional momentum/size book on liquid perps is a plausible but untested money route. Carry is not profitable at current funding (it roughly equals a cash yield).

verdicts.title: The variance skill has nothing to trade against: no implied volatility and no options venue
verdicts.corrected_evidence: vrp.py reproduces (DVOL 45.4 vs RV 44.1, +1.2 points, 56% of hours; 36.9 vs 32.5, +4.5 points, 70%; corr 0.27/0.18), and there is no IV input or options instrument in the repo. But the comparison mixes horizons: DVOL is a 30-day implied index and the RV is forward 24h, so the gap is not a tradeable variance-risk-premium estimate. Each set covers about one month (701/935 overlapping hourly points, which amounts to roughly 30-40 independent days).
verdicts.notes: The mechanism is right in principle: a variance forecast pays only against a market price of variance or as a sizing input. But the system's measured variance skill is at 1-15 min, with a 0.5-2.8% QLIKE gain over FHS. Option books price 1-day to 30-day variance, where HAR-type forecasts are public knowledge, and Deribit ATM spreads plus fees and delta-hedging costs are far larger than a few percent of QLIKE. IV>RV is a premium you can earn by plain short volatility, with no forecast needed and with crash risk; it is independent of neural_trade. The more relevant monetization of the variance skill is as the gate in blocker 4.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not from this model's skill: it is at the wrong horizon and far too small for option spreads. A generic short-vol (VRP) strategy might earn money, but it would not need this system.

blockers.title: Horizons are hard-wired to 1/5/15 min, where the round-trip cost eats 24-95% of the average move
blockers.evidence: model.py:58 HORIZON_STEPS=[1,5,15], model.py:41 LOOKBACK=60, model.py:48 MAX_SEQUENCE_COUNT=2880 (about 40 h of training). Measured on the 43,500-bar CSV: mean |log return| is 4.2/9.6/16.5/32.5/65.6/171.5 bps at 1/5/15/60/240/1440 min. Break-even accuracy is p*=0.5+c/(2E|r|). At 4 bps round trip (futures maker): 97.5%/70.9%/62.1%/56.2%/53.0%/51.2%. At 10 bps (futures taker): >100%/>100%/80.3%/65.4%/57.6%/52.9%. At 20 bps (spot): unreachable up to 15 min, 80.8% at 60 min, 55.8% at 1 day. The best published BTC direction accuracy at 1-15 min is 51-54% (report 10.3).
blockers.mechanism: Costs are a fixed toll on every trade, while the expected move grows with sqrt(h). At the horizons the architecture allows, no realistic accuracy covers the toll. At 4 h to 1 day the required accuracy falls into the range the literature reports. Nothing in the research ever tested h > 15 min, so the setup excludes the only horizons where a weak edge could pay.
blockers.fix_or_test: Run the existing harness (research/tsfm_eval/bench/metrics2.py: nonoverlap_trades plus the momentum, reversal and logreg baselines) at h in {60, 240, 1440} on multi-year data (the 2017-2025 file the notebook loaded, 4.6M rows). Score net of 10 bps. Make HORIZON_STEPS, LOOKBACK and the training window scale with h. Stop rule: if no baseline or model is positive net of 10 bps with a block-bootstrap CI excluding 0 on >= 6 months out of sample, drop directional trading.

blockers.title: The notebook backtest cannot measure PnL: no fees, look-ahead, fills on the signal's own close, and 11x hidden leverage
blockers.evidence: inference.ipynb cell 5 (execution count 5): line 196 np.convolve(mode='same') and line 197 rolling(center=True) use about 10 future bars, and the zero padding halves var_mean at the series edges. These centred values drive both the entry filter and the SPIKE exit (lines 269, 274, 278, 291). Lines 310-315 compute profit with no fees. Entry and exit fill at close=last_close_test (line 226), which is the same close the model just saw (lines 257, 285), so there is no latency. The loop stops 30 bars early and silently drops any open position (line 255). Cell 7 lines 17-24 add a profit per 1 BTC (about $114k notional) to a $10,000 account, which is 10.9x implicit leverage. The logged result is 9 trades, -$174. Fees on those 9 trades: spot 10+10 bps = $2,052, futures taker = $1,026, futures maker = $410. The real result is about -$2,226 (-22% of the stated account), not -1.7%.
blockers.mechanism: This is the only PnL path the SRS system has (FR-5, SRS 3.4). Its numbers are biased up by look-ahead and by zero costs, and the account-level percentage is mis-scaled by the 11x hidden leverage. Decisions made from it (thresholds, exits) are tuned on fiction.
blockers.fix_or_test: Replace it with an event-driven backtest. Decide at the close of t and fill at t+latency (or the open of t+1). Charge fees per venue and tier. Use trailing windows only. Mark open positions to market and close them at the end. Size notional from equity (units = risk budget / price). Re-run the 480-bar test: if it is not positive net of 4 bps, the notebook strategy is dead.

blockers.title: The entry and exit rules contradict the model's outputs: short-only by construction, a sign-blind unanimity filter, and holding 6x the forecast horizon
blockers.evidence: Cell 5 enters at dir_prob>0.65 or <0.35 (lines 274, 278). The direction head is centred at 0.31-0.44 (calibration 6; focal alpha 0.7, D3), so the backtest made 0 LONG and 9 SHORT trades. The reversal exits are asymmetric: a LONG would exit at <0.45, i.e. on almost every bar; a SHORT exits only at >0.55, which almost never happens, so shorts close on the look-ahead SPIKE exit or on TIME (lines 296-306). Agreement: max(up, 3-up)/3 >= 0.67 (line 186; helper_functions.py:88 has the same default). 2/3 = 0.6667 < 0.67, so the filter silently demands 3/3 agreement, and it never checks that the agreed sign matches the trade side, so a SHORT can enter when all three deltas point UP (lines 266-279). The primary signal is the 5-min head (line 84), but max_hold=30 bars (line 253).
blockers.mechanism: Trades are driven by the head's class bias and by look-ahead exits, not by a forecast. Holding 30 minutes on a 5-minute forecast adds 25 minutes of zero-mean noise per trade. That cuts the t-stat by about sqrt(6) and leaves the cost per trade unchanged.
blockers.fix_or_test: Use centred, causal rank thresholds (as in research/timestral_lig/calibrate.py). Require sign(agreement) == trade side, with an explicit k-of-3 count. Set the hold equal to the forecast horizon, or exit when the forecast for the position's side expires. Re-score on both Test sets net of 4 and 10 bps.

blockers.title: TP and SL exist only on paper, and their distances are far outside the 1-30 min move scale
blockers.evidence: Cell 5 lines 24-38: the TP1 +0.5%, TP2 +1.5% and SL -1% levels are 'not executed, just reference'. helper_functions.calculate_dynamic_stop_loss (lines 61-70) gives a stop 2%*(1+min(ratio,2)) = 2-6% away. helper_functions.py is imported by neither model.py, inference.ipynb nor test_model.py. FR-4.3, FR-4.4 and FR-5.3 (partial profit taking) are unimplemented. CSV, random entries, 30-bar window: +0.5% reached 10.9% (long) / 12.2% (short), +1.5% 0.4-0.5%, -1% 1.9%, -2% 0.13%, -4% and -6% never. With the brackets executed, 86-97% of trades still end on the time exit. An executed +0.5/-1% bracket needs 66.7% wins gross, 71.3% with a maker TP and taker SL (2+5 bps), and 80% at spot. Brackets do not create expectancy: every TP/SL variant tested on random entries had a gross E within +/-0.8 bps, the same as the time exit (-0.41).
blockers.mechanism: There is no working risk control: the stop sits 8-35 sigma away (report 8), so tail losses are unbounded in practice. The reported win rate is just a time-exit coin flip. The bracket design cannot rescue a no-edge signal, and as built it cannot even cap losses for one that has an edge.
blockers.fix_or_test: Express TP and SL in forecast-sigma units, e.g. FHS quantiles of the h-return (roughly 1.5-3 sigma, about 20-70 bps at 15 min). Execute them in the backtest with pessimistic intrabar ordering (same bar = SL first). Charge TP as maker and SL as taker. Compare drawdown and net PnL with and without the stop on any candidate signal.

blockers.title: No execution layer, and the research fill model is optimistic for the one pattern that depends on the first minute
blockers.evidence: SRS 10.3: 'No Live Trading Execution'; the system emits signals only. There are no limit orders, OCO, fee-tier or BNB logic. The research fills every trade at the forecast bar's close, with zero latency and certain fills, at 4 bps called 'futures maker' (metrics2.py:32, :126-133). CSV, fading the top 2% of |z15| (causal trailing-480 rank), hold 15 min, non-overlapping: gross per trade +1.62 bps at a 1-minute delay of 0, +1.09 at 1, +0.99 at 2 (1-min grid). On the 3-min grid: +2.73 at delay 0, +0.86 at 1, +0.41 at 2. Gross by hold time: 1 min +0.42, 3 min +1.21 (t = 2.0), 15 min +1.68, 60 min -0.48. Passive entries: a bid posted at the close is traded through within 1 min 85% of the time, then drifts -0.8 bps against the fill. The fade entered with limit orders 2-10 bps away fills 130-275 times and earns only +0.1 to +2.4 bps gross. Every execution variant is negative net of 4 bps.
blockers.mechanism: Costs are the binding constraint, yet the system has no way to obtain maker fees or to execute stops. The research cost model pairs maker fees with taker-like immediacy. 1-minute OHLC cannot resolve whether a reversal that starts inside the first minute survives real latency and queue position. So the most promising directional pattern is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
blockers.fix_or_test: Download Binance aggTrades and bookTicker (or perp equivalents) for both Test windows. Simulate a 100-1000 ms decision latency and maker fills with queue position and partial fills. Use maker-in/taker-out (about 7 bps on futures VIP0) as the central cost case. If the fade is not positive at 7 bps with real fills, close the short-horizon direction route for good.

blockers.title: Position sizing ignores the only measured skill (variance), and confidence is in scaler-dependent units
blockers.evidence: helper_functions.py:5 sets confidence = 1/(1+variance). Here the variance is the Student-t scale squared in SCALED units (model.py:120-121, :1700-1717), from a StandardScaler fitted on the 1/5/15-min deltas pooled together (model.py:377-382) and refitted on every run. On the CSV sd (6.4/14.1/23.8 bps, pooled 16.4) a correct head gives typical confidence 0.87/0.58/0.32 (0.95/0.80/0.59 if it learns the t scale with nu=3). The size multiplier steps 1.2/1.0/0.6 (helper_functions.py:77-84) therefore track the horizon, not market risk, and the conf>0.5 gate on the 5-min head (cell 5 line 274) sits on its typical value. The multiplier spans 2x, while hourly realised vol spans 5.4x (p5-p95: 2.1-11.5 bps per minute), 4.3x across days and 1.9x by hour of day. Log-vol hour-to-hour autocorrelation is 0.71. The notebook trades a constant 1 BTC.
blockers.mechanism: With constant units, PnL variance is concentrated in high-vol hours. Any edge measured in sigma units (like the z-scored reversal) is diluted, and drawdowns are set by the worst regime. The Timestral and FHS variance gain (QLIKE 0.5-2.8%, range 5-17%) has no consumer in the pipeline, so it cannot become money.
blockers.fix_or_test: Size each trade as units = risk budget (bps of equity) / sigma_FHS,h (bps), capped at a leverage limit. For a Kelly-style variant, size proportional to the expected edge / sigma^2. Re-run the deployed calibration rules and the fade with and without vol targeting, and compare Sharpe and max drawdown. This isolates what the variance skill is worth.

blockers.title: A full round trip is charged per forecast, not per position change
blockers.evidence: metrics2.py:126-133 (nonoverlap_trades), research/timestral_lig/trading_nocost.py and calibrate.py all close the position after h minutes and pay the full cost again, even when the next signal has the same side. Cell 5 does the same. neural_trade says DOWN at every origin in 13 of 18 runs (D3), so its net -1.1 to -4.6 bps per trade at 4 bps (T-D, 47-324 trades) is mostly the churn cost of re-opening a constant short. CSV: for sign signals on non-overlapping 15/60/240-min blocks, the next block has the same side 49-50% of the time.
blockers.mechanism: Holding the position when the next signal agrees would cut the number of round trips by about half for coin-flip-like signals, and by much more for persistent ones (trend, long-horizon). The research overstates the cost burden of any slow signal, which matters most for the longer horizons in blocker 1.
blockers.fix_or_test: Switch to a target-position backtest with a no-trade band (hysteresis). Charge cost on |change in position| only. Re-score the T-D, calibration and fade results; report the turnover and the net PnL change.

blockers.title: Test windows and trade counts are too small to detect any realistic edge
blockers.evidence: Deployed calibration rules had 29-107 Test trades (calibration 4.1). The month-long CSV fade has 212-306. Minimum detectable accuracy (one-sided 5%, 80% power): 73.1% at n=29, 62.0% at n=107, 57.1% at n=306. Trades needed: 616 for 55%, 1,715 for 53%, 3,862 for 52%. Test windows were 6 and 14 days on a 3-minute origin grid (2,895 and 6,715 origins). The top-2% fade gives about 10 trades per day, so a 53% edge needs about 170 days.
blockers.mechanism: The 'no edge' verdicts can only exclude edges of 60% and above. The plausible 52-55% range stays untested, so a real but small edge would be thrown away. Combined with the 1-15 min horizons, such an edge would lose after costs anyway, which reinforces blocker 1.
blockers.fix_or_test: Pre-register one rule. Evaluate on >= 6 months of 1-minute origins, using overlapping trades with a block bootstrap or HAC errors instead of non-overlap thinning. State the target edge and the power before scoring.

blockers.title: Venue mismatch: spot data, futures fees, short trades and no funding
blockers.evidence: dw_ccxt.py:14 and :48 use ccxt.binance (spot) and 'BTC/USDT'. The research charges futures fees: 4 bps maker and 10 bps taker per round trip (metrics2.py:32). All 9 notebook trades are SHORT. Shorting on spot needs margin borrowing, which carries interest and 10 bps per side, and perp funding every 8 h is not modelled. At spot costs (20 bps) almost no forecast clears the cost (report 7.7).
blockers.mechanism: The backtested PnL is not achievable on the venue whose prices it uses. The cheap cost case (4 bps) assumes a perp account, a fee tier and funding that the data and code never model.
blockers.fix_or_test: Choose the venue: the USDS-M perp, using its klines, funding history and the account's fee tier, or long-only spot at 15-20 bps. Re-run the cost tables on that venue's own prices.

verdicts.title: Horizons are hard-wired to 1/5/15 min, where the round-trip cost eats 24-95% of the average move
verdicts.corrected_evidence: I re-measured the CSV and the numbers match: mean |log r| is 4.2/9.6/16.5/32.5/65.6/171.5 bps at 1/5/15/60/240/1440 min. The 1440-min value rests on only 30 independent days. Two corrections. (a) The horizons are not hard-wired. Config.RESAMPLE_MINUTES (model.py:43, applied at :219-233) already resamples the bars. Setting it to 60 gives 1/5/15-HOUR horizons with a 60 h lookback and 2,880 sequences (about 120 days of hourly training), with no code change. The restriction that is really fixed is in the research harness: research/tsfm_eval/bench/common.py:19 sets HORIZONS=[1,5,15], and calibrate.py uses the same HS. No test anywhere used h>15 min, so that part of the claim holds. (b) The formula p*=0.5+c/(2E|r|) assumes |r| does not depend on whether the call is right, so it overstates the accuracy needed. If signal and return are jointly Gaussian, the break-even IC is c/E|r| and p*=0.5+arcsin(IC)/pi. At 15 min/4 bps that gives 57.8% (not 62.1%); at 60 min/10 bps, 60.0% (not 65.4%); at 240 min/10 bps, 54.9% (IC 0.15); at 1 day/10 bps, 51.9% (IC 0.058). The true value lies between the two models. Either way, at 1-15 min no plausible IC covers even 4 bps (IC 0.24 needed at 15 min).
verdicts.notes: This is the only blocker in the list that addresses the binding constraint: gross edge per trade is far below cost. Every other execution fix leaves a gross edge of 0-3 bps against a 4-10 bps toll. The mechanism is right but needs a caveat. A lower break-even is necessary, not sufficient. What matters is whether the IC decays more slowly than 1/sqrt(h). At 1 day the required IC (about 0.04-0.06) falls in the range reported for crypto trend and time-series momentum signals. At 4 h, 0.15 is still very demanding. Two costs grow with h and are missing from the evidence: funding (about 1 bps per 8 h, about 3 bps/day, borne mainly by longs) and statistical power. The proposed stop rule ('>=6 months OOS') is underpowered at h=1 day: about 180 trades gives a minimum detectable accuracy near 59%. Use a walk-forward over the full 2017-2025 file (about 3,200 daily blocks; that file is gitignored as Bitcoin_BTCUSDT.csv and not in this checkout, so it was not tested here). Pair it with position-change cost accounting.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: Only together with a signal that has a real IC at 4 h-1 day (e.g. trend/TSMOM, tested over multiple years), cost charged per position change (blocker 7), and funding modelled (blocker 9). It is the necessary precondition, not a profit source by itself.

verdicts.title: The notebook backtest cannot measure PnL: no fees, look-ahead, fills on the signal's own close, and 11x hidden leverage
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: there are no fees (cell 5 lines 310-315). Cell 7 lines 17-24 add a 1-BTC PnL to a $10k account; mean price is $114,138, so the implicit leverage is 11.4x. The fee arithmetic checks out: entry plus exit notional over the 9 trades is $2,053,666, so fees are $2,054 at spot, $1,027 at futures taker and $411 at maker. The net result is about -$2,228 (-22%), not -$174. The look-ahead is immaterial in the logged run. I decoded the plotly payload in cell 7: all 9 exits are 'TIME', so the SPIKE exit never fired. With variance recovered from confidence (var=1/conf-1), the centred var_mean flags spikes only at bars 0-1 (the zero-padding edge effect). The trailing version flags 3 bars. Both give the same 74 entry-eligible bars, and replays without the agreement filter give gross -$396 (centred) vs -$391 (trailing). var_std (rolling center=True, line 197) is never used in the trading loop, only stored in the DataFrame (line 236). Filling at last_close is the standard close-to-close assumption, not look-ahead. Unconfirmed: whether a position was dropped at the end of the loop.
verdicts.notes: All the biases point in the optimistic direction, and the result is already negative before fees. So this defect hides losses, not money. A larger problem the critic missed: the 480-bar window is also the validation set (D4, model.py:728-731) and covers only 8 h with 9 trades. No fix makes it a valid out-of-sample test. The proposed decision rule ('re-run the 480-bar test, positive net of 4 bps or dead') is uninformative either way at n=9. The research harness (metrics2.py, calibrate.py) has already replaced it.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. It would only make the loss visible (about -22% of the stated account at spot fees instead of -1.7%). It is a measurement fix, not a profit route.

verdicts.title: The entry and exit rules contradict the model's outputs: short-only by construction, a sign-blind unanimity filter, and holding 6x the forecast horizon
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Decoded outputs: the 5-min direction head ranges 0.140-0.494 (median 0.402). LONG (>0.65) and the SHORT reversal exit (>0.55) can never fire, giving 0 LONG and 9 SHORT. dp<0.35 holds on 123/480 bars. The conf>0.5 gate passes 431/480 bars, so it barely binds. The agreement threshold: 2/3=0.6667<0.67, so the filter demands 3/3 (cell 5 line 186; helper_functions.py:88 has the same default). It accepts unanimous UP deltas for a SHORT; confirmed from the code. Whether this happened cannot be checked, because the delta predictions are not in the saved outputs. Correction: shorts did not close on the look-ahead SPIKE exit. All 9 exits were TIME at exactly 30 bars.
verdicts.notes: The proposed fix (centred, causal rank thresholds; side-consistent agreement) is essentially what research/timestral_lig/calibrate.py already ran. It uses confidence 'dp' = direction head minus its calibration median, causal trailing-480 ranks and 'agree3' sign-consistent alignment. It found no rule above 50% out of sample, and agree3 changed accuracy by at most 4.4 points, more often down. The head's MCC is about 0 (report 7.9). The sqrt(6) t-stat argument holds only if an edge exists at 5 min, and none was measured. With fixed costs, a longer hold actually lowers the cost per unit of risk.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. The corrected rule was already tested in the calibration study and failed; the head has no directional skill to unlock.

verdicts.title: TP and SL exist only on paper, and their distances are far outside the 1-30 min move scale
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: the levels are reference-only (cell 5 lines 24-38). calculate_dynamic_stop_loss gives 2-6% (helper_functions.py:61-75). helper_functions.py is imported nowhere; the notebook redefines its own helpers. I re-measured on the CSV (30-bar window, random entries): +0.5% is reached 10.95%/12.22% (up/down), 1% 1.9%, 1.5% 0.4-0.6%, 2% 0.08-0.10%, 4% never. Overstated: 'tail losses are unbounded in practice'. The 30-bar time exit already bounds them. The worst 30-min adverse low in the month was -2.47%, and p99.9 was -1.99%. The real tail risk is the 11.4x implicit notional (a 2.5% move is about 28% of the $10k account), which is a sizing problem, not a missing stop.
verdicts.notes: The critic correctly concedes that brackets cannot create expectancy (optional stopping on a near-martingale; random-entry variants within +/-0.8 bps). Executing stops on 1-min bars adds taker fills, which raises costs for a cost-bound strategy. Sigma-scaled brackets are reasonable risk hygiene once an edge exists.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. Brackets reshape the payoff distribution but not its mean; the loss is already capped by the time exit.

verdicts.title: No execution layer, and the research fill model is optimistic for the one pattern that depends on the first minute
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: there is no execution layer (SRS 10.3), and metrics2.py:32/:126-133 fills at the forecast close with 4 bps labelled 'maker'. I replicated the fade (EWMA-sigma z of the 15-min return, top 2% trailing-480 rank, fade, hold 15, non-overlapping) on the CSV. 1-min grid: gross +1.72/+1.37/+1.04 bps at delay 0/1/2 (n=299, t=1.15/0.90/0.73). 3-min grid: +2.77/+1.20/+0.92 (n=208, t=1.42 at delay 0). By hold time: 1 min +0.38, 3 min +1.21 (t 1.99), 15 min +1.72, 30 min +0.84, 60 min -0.37. This matches the critic within about 0.3-0.5 bps.
verdicts.notes: The conclusion 'neither confirmed nor ruled out' is too generous. The zero-latency, certain-fill, close-price number is already an upper bound for any execution after the signal bar, and it is +1.7 bps gross (+2.8 at best on the 3-min grid). That is below the cheapest retail round trip (4 bps maker/maker) and far below maker-in/taker-out (about 7 bps). Tick data would matter only for a maker-rebate or market-maker tier, where adverse selection (the critic's own -0.8 bps drift after passive fills) eats the edge. Tick-level work is not worth its cost for this pattern. The research cost model is optimistic, which makes the existing negative verdict stronger, not weaker.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No at retail fee tiers: the gross upper bound is 1.7-2.8 bps against 4-7 bps of cost. It would matter only with a rebate tier plus a signal with more than about 3 bps of gross edge, and none exists.

verdicts.title: Position sizing ignores the only measured skill (variance), and confidence is in scaler-dependent units
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: confidence=1/(1+var) uses scaled units (helper_functions.py:5; target scaler pooled over horizons at model.py:377-382). The notebook's 5-min confidence median is 0.593 (critic predicted 0.58), and the conf>0.5 gate passes 90% of bars. Hourly realized vol is p5-p95 2.18-11.67 bps/min (5.4x). The size multiplier lives in unused code (helper_functions.py is never imported); the notebook trades 1 BTC.
verdicts.notes: The proposed fix (units = budget / sigma_h) points the wrong way for a strategy where costs bind. With a fixed bps cost, net per unit under 1/sigma sizing is edge_z - c/sigma, which overweights low-vol trades, where cost/move is worst. I tested this on the CSV fade at 4 bps: constant size -2.28 bps per unit-trade, 1/sigma sizing -2.81, sigma-proportional -1.90. By sigma tercile at entry: low -2.24, mid -3.82, high -0.80 net. So vol-gating (trade only when forecast sigma is large relative to cost) is the right consumer of the variance skill, and it is still negative here. The Timestral gain over FHS (QLIKE 0.5-2.8%) is too small to change any sizing decision. FHS gives almost the same sigma for free, so the incremental money from the 'only measured skill' in this role is about 0. Monetising variance skill would need a volatility instrument (options, straddles, market-making spread setting), which nobody has proposed or tested.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. Vol targeting improves the Sharpe of an existing edge but cannot create one, and with fixed bps costs it lowered net PnL on the only candidate signal (-2.28 to -2.81 bps per unit-trade). It would matter only together with a positive-net signal, using sigma as a gate rather than a divisor.

verdicts.title: A full round trip is charged per forecast, not per position change
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: nonoverlap_trades (metrics2.py:126-138) and trade_index in calibrate.py charge a full round trip per trade. Mechanism corrected: T-D trades the point forecast (q-median sign with |pred| > cost), not the direction head. Point signs are often one-sided (100% short in several h=5 runs). On the 3-min origin grid, back-to-back trades at h=1 and h=5 are impossible, so the 'constant short churn' explanation fails there. I re-scored all 14 repo-set neural_trade T-D cells (n>=20) with a target-position backtest, charging cost on |change in position|. Round trips fell by 0-60% (most at h=15, e.g. 254 to 130). Net improved in every cell, but 11 of 14 stay negative, and the 3 that turn positive (asis seed 0 h=15 +346 bps; rolling seed 1 h=15 +71; asis seed 1 h=15 +361, which was already positive) are the repo-set h=15 cells that report 4.8 shows reversing on the clean set. On the clean set, 8 of 8 cells stay negative (e.g. -1,450 to -1,294 bps; -706 to -585 bps).
verdicts.notes: The accounting really is conservative, and standard practice charges cost per position change. The saving scales with signal persistence, so it matters for slow (long-horizon or trend) signals and hardly at all for the top-2% fade, whose signals rarely occur back-to-back. It adds drift exposure when the position is held through gaps, which must be benchmarked against always-long or always-short.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No on its own (clean set: 8/8 still negative). Only together with a persistent long-horizon signal (blocker 1), where it could cut costs by more than half.

verdicts.title: Test windows and trade counts are too small to detect any realistic edge
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Arithmetic confirmed (one-sided 5%, 80% power): n=616 for 55%, 1,715 for 53%, 3,862 for 52%, 288 for 57.3%. The deployed calibration rules had 29-107 Test trades (trading_calibration.md section 1). The Test windows were 6 and 14 days. Context missing from the critic's evidence: the short windows were imposed by Timestral's 2026-10-15 release date (contamination control, common.py POST_START). They are needed for zero-shot TSFMs but not for price-only baselines or neural_trade, which could have been scored on the 8.75-year 2017-2025 file the notebook loads (4,598,198 rows; not in this checkout).
verdicts.notes: The power gap is real but is not a profit blocker at 1-15 min. Even under the Gaussian break-even, the cheapest case (15 min, 4 bps) needs 57.8%, which these tests could detect, so a hidden 52-55% edge there would lose anyway. Power becomes binding exactly where blocker 1 points (4 h-1 day, break-even about 52-55%). Note on the fix: overlapping trades with HAC errors add little information. Effective sample size is still about T/h, so the answer is more calendar time (multi-year walk-forward), not denser origins.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No on its own. It is required together with blocker 1, to detect or reject a 52-55% edge at 4 h-1 day horizons.

verdicts.title: Venue mismatch: spot data, futures fees, short trades and no funding
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: dw_ccxt.py:14 ccxt.binance (spot) and :48 'BTC/USDT'; metrics2.py:32 COSTS=[4,10,20] are labelled futures maker/taker and spot. Funding at about 0.01%/8 h is about 0.03 bps per 15-min hold, negligible at the tested horizons. Spot-perp return differences at 1-15 min are small next to 4-20 bps of cost.
verdicts.notes: The impact is low at the tested horizons and becomes material only at 4 h-1 day, where funding adds about 1-3 bps per position and taxes longs. Venue and fee tier is the largest lever on the cost side, but even zero fees do not rescue any signal tested: report timestral_lig 4.8 shows no-commission PnL with |t|<2 for all models, and the fade is +1.7 bps gross with t of about 1.2.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No on its own. It matters only together with a long-horizon signal (funding) or as a cost reduction for a signal whose gross edge already exceeds about 4 bps, and none does.

blockers.title: Every decision rule keys on the median, the output with no skill. The spread/range, the output with skill, never sets expected value.
blockers.evidence: Rules tested so far: sign of median with a 0.01 bps no-call band (research/timestral_lig/trading_nocost.py:20-33; calibrate.py:39,113); |median| > cost (model_evaluation_timestral.md 7.7, T-D). Calibration confidences are all scale-free: z = median/(IQR/1.349), pm = P(up)-0.5, dp, then a percentile rank over the trailing 480 origins (calibrate.py:6-9, 82-85, 116-118). Bps magnitude never enters. Variance skill measured but unused: QLIKE 0.5-2.8% better than FHS; range forecast 5-17% better than EWMA (eval 7.2, 7.5). On the CSV, a free causal Parkinson-EWMA vol forecast ranks |r| with Spearman 0.36-0.40. Break-even accuracy at 4 bps by predicted-vol decile (cut points over the whole month, descriptive): h=15 78.7% (D1) -> 56.8% (D10), 56.1% in the top 2%; h=5 100% -> 61.6%; h=1 at least 75% in every decile (scratchpad/obj/a1.py). In T-D, better-calibrated models (Timestral ctx2048) make 0-46 trades, while noisy-median models trade most and lose most (Chronos-Bolt: 394-490 trades, -4.2 to -5.2 bps per trade, t down to -8.0).
blockers.mechanism: Net EV per trade is about (2p-1)*E|r| - c. Only E|r| is predictable. Scale-free ranking divides it out, so rules are selected on the noise dimension (direction) and pay costs equally in quiet regimes, where no hit rate can cover them. A |median|>c gate measures how noisy the median is, not EV. A vol gate alone is not enough: on the CSV, fading every 15-min move goes from -0.31 bps gross per trade (low-vol tercile) to +0.30 (high-vol tercile), and E|r|>=20 bps cuts net loss from -11,317 to -2,067 bps but stays negative (a4.py). The gate is necessary, and it must be paired with a direction signal of at least 57-60%.
blockers.fix_or_test: Pre-register one EV rule with no searched parameters: trade iff (2*p_hat - 1)*Ehat|r_h| > c. Ehat|r_h| comes from FHS or Timestral quantiles (mean |q|). p_hat comes from a walk-forward, isotonic-calibrated logistic (6-feature base model, eval 7.6) or a fixed reversal prior estimated only on pre-period data. Ablation: the same rule with a constant Ehat|r| isolates what the variance forecast adds. Also pre-register the combination the research already flagged: fade top-2% |z| moves only when Ehat|r_15| >= 20 bps. On this month, in-sample and overlapping the repo Test window, that is n=50, 64% hit, +8.0 bps net per trade, against -1.05 without the gate. That figure is motivation, not evidence. Score once on months of unseen data (see the power blocker).

blockers.title: The research protocol cannot detect a profitable edge: 6-14 day windows, small top-k samples and a max-over-rules gate
blockers.evidence: dw_ccxt.py:31 hard-codes 30 days of data; model.py:48 MAX_SEQUENCE_COUNT=2,880 (2 days); Test windows are 6 and 14 days. The P-B calibration (the only one for neural_trade) uses 3-7 days. Deployed rules had 29-107 trades. One-sided binomial power at alpha 0.05 for a true 60% rule (about break-even at h=15 in high vol): 0.29/0.34/0.62 at n=30/50/100. Trades needed for 80% power: 160 (60%), 245 (58%), 620 (55%). With Holm over 6 rules, power at 60% is 0.09-0.31 for n=30-100. Gate: the null-max median of the R-rule search in calibration.json is 0.54-0.58. A simulation matched to that gives power 0.18-0.31 to deploy a true 60% rule at n=100 and 0.38-0.54 for a 63% rule. Joint gate x Test power is about 5-20%. For a PnL t of 1.96: 14 days needs annualised Sharpe 10.0, 6 days 15.3, 90 days 3.9, one year 2.0.
blockers.mechanism: 'No rule passed' is the expected result even if a cost-covering 58-60% rule existed. Pushing to the top 1-2% to maximise accuracy shrinks n further. The protocol can certify only Sharpe of about 10 or more, so profitable Sharpe 2-5 strategies stay invisible and get labelled 'no edge'.
blockers.fix_or_test: Download 2-4 years of 1-min BTCUSDT (free; about 1M bars; parameterise dw_ccxt.py:31). Run walk-forward with monthly refits and a purge. Use every origin with staggered overlapping 1/h positions and Newey-West SEs instead of greedy non-overlapping top-k trades. Pre-register at most 3 rules. State the target before testing, e.g. 80% power for Sharpe 3, which needs about 156 trading days of forward or untouched history.

blockers.title: Accuracy is the optimisation target, but money depends on E[d*r] - c
blockers.evidence: The task in plans/trading_calibration.md:6 reads 'maximise accuracy at the expense of trading volume'. Scoring uses the Wilson LB of accuracy (W) or raw accuracy (R) and drops zero-return trades (calibrate.py:135-140). The deployed clean P-A price-only rule had 56.1% accuracy and lost -226 bps gross and -658 net (trading_calibration.md:93). For the top-2% 5-min fade the average loss is 14.5 bps against an average win of 7.4, so break-even is 59-85% (lines 137-138). Same pattern on the CSV: the top-2% 15-min fade wins 60.1% of trades, but the average loss is 21.1 bps against an average win of 18.9 bps, so it nets -1.05 bps per trade.
blockers.mechanism: Accuracy ignores payoff size. Fading after large moves has negative skew: continuations are the big losers. Maximising accuracy therefore selects negatively skewed rules that lose money. Cutting volume does not cut cost per trade, but it does cut statistical power.
blockers.fix_or_test: Select and gate on mean net PnL per trade at 4 and 10 bps (its lower CI bound, or HAC t), with the same label-shift null. Report accuracy only as a description. If payoff shaping (vol-scaled stop, horizon) is wanted, pre-register it as part of the rule and do not search it.

blockers.title: neural_trade's losses build in a short bias, and the decision layer turns it into a bet on market direction
blockers.evidence: Focal alpha=0.7 on DOWN, gamma=1 (model.py:113-114; math_helpers.py:132). With P(up)=0.5, the loss-optimal constant output is 0.383. The head exceeds 0.5 only if true P(up) >= 0.70, and exceeds the notebook LONG threshold 0.65 only if P(up) >= 0.875. SHORT (< 0.35) fires once P(up) <= 0.437. The 5-min head uses pinball tau=0.4 (model.py:78, 1460) with lambda_point clamped at 1000: the sign of its median is DOWN in 12 of 12 runs (mean up-share 0.278, min 0.000), against 0.509 and 0.485 at 1 and 15 min (trading_nocost.json). Direction-head PnL equals exactly -(always long) in 18 of 36 cells. The only nominally significant neural_trade result (clean, h=1, +763.9 bps, t=2.04) came in a -528 bps market. The stored notebook run made 9 trades: 0 LONG, 9 SHORT. The alignment loss (model.py:1735-1767) pulls the head toward a Gaussian P(up) built from the biased mu. Labels use ret > 0, so zero returns (1.9% at 1 min) count as DOWN (model.py:1614).
blockers.mechanism: Decisions measure the window's drift, not a forecast. PnL sign follows the market, there is no gross edge to cover costs, and every backtest of this model is confounded by trend.
blockers.fix_or_test: Use alpha=0.5 (plain BCE) and tau=0.5, or drop the point head. Centre decisions on an isotonic-calibrated P(up) fitted on past data. Report every PnL next to always-long and always-short, plus a drift-hedged PnL. Pass check after retraining: head up-share close to the realised up-share, and correlation of strategy PnL with always-long close to 0.

blockers.title: The decision layer treats high predicted variance as risk to avoid, which inverts the cost logic (sizing, spike filter, stops)
blockers.evidence: inference.ipynb cell 5: entry needs conf=1/(1+v) > 0.5 and no spike (lines 198, 274, 278), and a spike forces an exit (lines 291-293). helper_functions.py:77-86 sizes 1.2x when confidence > 0.7 (low variance) and 0.6x when confidence <= 0.5. SRS FR-4.2, FR-4.6. On the CSV (a3.py), the causal spike flag (v > 2x trailing 20-bar mean; 2.4% of origins) has break-even at 4 bps of 62.9% (h=5) and 59.0% (h=15), against 71.3% and 62.3% without a spike. The low-vol tercile, which gets the larger size, needs 85.7% and 69.8%; the high-vol tercile, which gets the smaller size, needs 64.1% and 58.5%. Stop = 2%*(1+ratio) = 200-600 bps (helper_functions.py:61-75) against a 15-min sigma of 17-26 bps, so it never triggers. TP/SL at +0.5/+1.5/-1% are 'not executed, just reference' (cell 5 lines 24-38).
blockers.mechanism: The rules trade more and larger where costs cannot be covered, and skip the regimes where they can. Kelly-style sizing f ~ (mu-c)/sigma^2 is zero in low vol. There is no payoff shaping, because the exits are set in percent, not in volatility units.
blockers.fix_or_test: Replace with an EV abstain rule plus size proportional to max(0,(2p_hat-1)*Ehat|r| - c)/sigma_hat^2, capped. Set stops and targets from forecast quantiles (for example q05/q95 of h-min returns, in bps). Test inside the pre-registered walk-forward above, against the same rule with constant size.

blockers.title: Timestral-LIG was trained to have no direction, then judged on direction. Its variance objective is not weighted by decisions.
blockers.evidence: Design choices: a median random-walk penalty (timestral_lig.md:139; governed weight 6.6 -> 5.0, line 301), a recalibration G that shrinks the median 76-82% at h=1 and 100% from h=3-4 (line 38), and symmetric averaging of x and -x (line 98). As a result A1 and A2 make 'no calls' at h=5 and h=15 (lines 330-337), and the calibration grid was effectively 30-60 rules. Pass rule and V2 score: QLIKE plus pinball, unit-free and averaged over all origins. Symmetric averaging forces an even variance and an odd median. On the CSV (in-sample, one month, a2.py), after top-2% 15-min moves, realised/EWMA-predicted variance is 3.05 after DOWN moves and 2.15 after UP moves (leverage term -0.149*min(z,0)), and there is an even drift term of +0.36*|z| bps. The architecture cannot represent either.
blockers.mechanism: The model's only skill (magnitude) was scored on an average that weights quiet origins, where no trade can clear cost, as heavily as active ones. Its money use (as an E|r| input to a cost gate) was never tested, so a small real edge was judged as an 'adapter FAIL'. Asymmetric volatility information is removed by construction.
blockers.fix_or_test: Re-score A0, A2, C-FHS-hi and FHS on decision-relevant targets: Brier/AUC for the event |r_h| > c (c = 4 and 10 bps), Spearman of the predicted scale with |r| within the top two deciles, and the net PnL of the pre-registered EV-gate rule with each model's Ehat|r|. Run a paired ablation with symmetric averaging off for the variance path, with QLIKE tested conditionally on the sign of the last 15-min move.

blockers.title: Labels and losses ignore costs: deadband 0, sub-cost noise dominates the labels, and an anti-shrinkage penalty
blockers.evidence: Config.DIR_DEADBAND_BPS = 0.0 (model.py:119), although the masking code exists (model.py:1600-1616). On the CSV, the share of moves with |r| <= 4 bps is 62.8% at 1 min, 33.7% at 5 min and 19.8% at 15 min; with |r| <= 10 bps it is 91.3%, 66.3% and 45.0%. No loss term in model.py mentions cost, fee or PnL. vol_loss = |std(pred_h1) - std(actual)| (model.py:1769-1787, LAMBDA_VOL=1, line 73) pushes forecast dispersion up to the realised dispersion of a near-martingale target. T-D: neural_trade makes 81-324 trades with |forecast| > 4 bps, at -3.5 to -4.7 bps per trade (t down to -6.1).
blockers.mechanism: Model capacity goes to the sign of moves that cannot be traded profitably. The point forecast's magnitude is not an EV estimate, so cost-gated rules fire on noise.
blockers.fix_or_test: Set the deadband to the round-trip cost (a 3-class target with an abstain class, plain CE), or train directly on a differentiable net utility: mean(tanh(f)*r) - c*mean|delta tanh(f)| on vol-normalised returns. Drop vol_loss. Compare by walk-forward against the FHS-gated price-only baseline, with the same pre-registered scoring.

blockers.title: Monetisation routes that do not need direction are untested, and the data and scope restrictions rule them out
blockers.evidence: The measured skill is short-horizon magnitude. At 1 min the range forecast is 5.1-7.5% better than an EWMA of the range and 28-52% better than bias-corrected HAR (eval 7.5). SRS 10.3 states a single pair, no execution module, and OHLCV only (FR-1.1). Every test assumes a fill at the bar close (taker-like) while charging the 4 bps maker round trip (eval 7.7). No limit-order or passive execution was ever simulated, and no implied-vol data was used.
blockers.mechanism: A quoting or passive-execution engine earns the spread and pays maker fees. Its main input is the expected next-minute range, which is exactly where the model beats the baselines. A variance edge can also time variance-risk-premium trades. None of these routes needs a direction hit rate above 50%, but the research only priced directional taker trades.
blockers.fix_or_test: Record Binance L2 and trades through the free websocket for 4+ weeks. Simulate passive quotes at plus/minus k*sigma_hat_1min with conservative queue and fill rules. Measure spread capture minus adverse selection, using the range forecaster against an EWMA (paired). Separately, backtest a Deribit straddle rule on (implied - forecast) variance with Ehat from FHS or Timestral.

blockers.title: Model selection and stopping have no link to money, and the validation fold is also the test fold
blockers.evidence: In training_log.csv rows 0-8, val_loss is 4589.5-4590.3, of which 4586.72 is the constant, zero-gradient val_trend_loss (99.9%). Checkpoint and restore use val_loss (model.py:819-820). es_mcc has patience 15 > EPOCHS 8 (model.py:45, 821-823), so it never fires. In most epochs val_dir_acc_h1 = 0.4948 with MCC 0.000: a constant classifier, so accuracy is just the base rate. Rows 0-12 show acc 1.0 with MCC 0 (one-class validation). Price-space R2 and MAPE are reported and are trivially high. The 480-sample validation fold also serves as the test fold (D4).
blockers.mechanism: Weights are picked on noise in a loss that cannot tell a short-beta classifier from a skilled one. Every logged metric is biased by selection and has no relation to PnL.
blockers.fix_or_test: Select checkpoints on purged walk-forward validation blocks, separate from test, using a proper score (log loss of a calibrated P(up), QLIKE of the variance) and the net PnL of the pre-registered rule. Drop price-level R2 and MAPE from reports.

blockers.title: The notebook strategy's horizon, holding period and exits do not match the forecasts
blockers.evidence: In inference.ipynb cell 5, max_hold is 30 bars (line 253), longer than the longest forecast horizon (15). Entry and exit use only the 5-min head (line 84), which is the always-DOWN tau=0.4 head. The REV exit is asymmetric under the focal bias: LONG exits when head < 0.45 (true P(up) <= 0.62, almost at once), SHORT exits only when head > 0.55 (P(up) >= 0.77). weighted_sig weights horizons by config LAMBDA_SHORT/POINT/LONG (1/1/1, not even the calibrated 1000) and is only plotted (cell 7 lines 213-226). The cell 7 summary text says thresholds of 0.25/0.75, but the code uses 0.65/0.35. There are no fees (lines 310-315), and var_mean/var_std use centred windows (lines 196-197).
blockers.mechanism: Positions are held where no forecast exists, exits follow the bias rather than the information, and the horizon with any hint of structure (15-min reversal) is not the one traded.
blockers.fix_or_test: Choose h* = argmax_h[(2p_hat_h - 1)*Ehat|r_h| - c] at each origin and hold exactly h* bars. Allow no head-flip exits unless they are pre-registered. Use trailing windows only, and charge fees.

blockers.title: The trend and coherence prior points the wrong way for this market
blockers.evidence: model.py:1644-1676: the extended trend prior is the squared gap between the future delta and the past pct_change times price (a momentum prior), plus a sign-coherence penalty across horizons. It now has zero gradient (D2). The data reverse: momentum 'follow' trades were right less than 50% of the time in 73 of 80 cells (trading_calibration.md:116). On the CSV, the OLS slope of the future return on past z is -0.17 (H=5) and -0.39 (H=15).
blockers.mechanism: If someone 'fixes' D2 by making the term act on predictions, it will pull forecasts toward continuation, the opposite of the only stable pattern, and add anti-skill.
blockers.fix_or_test: Delete the term; do not repair it. If a trend prior is wanted, make it a learned signed feature, validated walk-forward.

verdicts.title: Every decision rule keys on the median, the output with no skill. The spread/range, the output with skill, never sets expected value.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: Only together with a direction signal that is right at least 57-60% of the time in high volatility (the 15-min reversal is the only candidate), maker-level costs, and a multi-year out-of-sample pass. A volatility gate alone does not help: on the CSV, fading every 15-min move gains only 0.6 bps gross per trade with the E|r|>=20 gate (-0.04 -> +0.58), against a 4 bps cost.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: I reproduced the numbers in a1/a4: decile break-evens, Spearman 0.36-0.40, top-2% fade n=268 at -1.05 net, and n=50 at +8.04 net with the E|r|>=20 gate. Three corrections. (a) The claim that 'bps magnitude never enters' is wrong for T-D. Its |median|>c rule is a bps EV gate. For a coherent distributional model, (2p-1)*E|r| is roughly proportional to |median| (Gaussian: about 0.64*|mu|). So the proposed EV rule with the model's own p_hat roughly reproduces T-D, which abstained correctly (Timestral ctx2048: 0/11/46 trades). Only calibrate.py is scale-free (rank on z/pm/dp, lines 62, 84). (b) (2p-1)*E|r| overstates EV when payoffs are skewed, which is the critic's own blocker 3. For the top-2% 15-min fade it predicts about 4.0 bps (p=0.601, E|r| about 19.8), but realised gross was 2.95. Use E[d*r|x] directly. (c) Rescaling alone does not help: ranking the fade by |past move in bps| instead of |z| gave +2.27 vs +2.95 gross (H=15, top 2%). What is new and untested is combining an independent direction prior with an external volatility level. A 48-cell grid on the CSV (scratchpad/obj/v_combo.py): at H=15, keep top 2-5% |z| and E|r|>=15-30 bps, all 12 of 12 cells are positive net of 4 bps (e.g. top 5%, E|r|>=20: n=99, 60.6% hit, +8.95 net, t=2.82). In the second half only 8 of 12 are positive. At H=5 the results are unstable, and at 10 bps cost the best cells fall to +2 to +4 bps.
verdicts.notes: The core idea is right: combine a direction prior with a volatility level, and score money in bps. The framing overstates it, because the median gate is already an EV gate for calibrated models. The grid evidence is in-sample, covers one month, and overlaps the repo Test window. It is still the only rule family that looks worth pre-registering. Specify it as E[d*r | z-bucket, vol-bucket] estimated on pre-period data, not as (2p-1)*E|r|.

verdicts.title: The research protocol cannot detect a profitable edge: 6-14 day windows, small top-k samples and a max-over-rules gate
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. It cannot create an edge, but it is the precondition for finding or killing one. It is also the cheapest decisive step: free Binance 1-min history from 2017 onward is a holdout that none of this research has touched.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: The binomial power figures are confirmed: 0.291/0.336/0.623 at n=30/50/100 for a 60% rule. With alpha/6 (the first Holm step) they are 0.094/0.156/0.307. Trades needed for 80% power: 158 at 60%, 245 at 58%, 620 at 55%. Sharpe needed for t=1.96: 15.3 over 6 days, 10.0 over 14 days, 3.9 over 90 days, 2.0 over a year. One error: '80% power for Sharpe 3 needs about 156 days' is wrong. 156 days is the 50%-power point for a two-sided test. 80% power needs about 251 days one-sided and 318 days two-sided; for Sharpe 5 it needs 90-115 days. The restriction is written into the code and the SRS: dw_ccxt.py:31 (30 days), model.py:48 (2,880 sequences) and SRS NFR-4.1 ('up to 2880 samples'). trading_calibration.md section 6 still proposes scoring the rule on '4 weeks of new data'. That gives about 50-100 trades, so the power is again only 0.3-0.6. Scale check: the vol-gated fade makes about 50-100 trades a month with a per-trade std of about 42 bps. Two years gives about 1,200-2,400 trades, so the SE is about 1 bps per trade. That is decisive for a +4 bps edge.
verdicts.notes: I would rank this first. It is cheap: parameterise the download, about 1M bars. It is decisive in both directions. It also turns the 'motivation' cells of blocker 1 into a real test. Use pre-2025-10 history as the untouched holdout, and pre-register at most 2-3 rules scored on net PnL with HAC SEs.

verdicts.title: Accuracy is the optimisation target, but money depends on E[d*r] - c
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. The deployed rules mostly lost gross because their accuracy itself fell to 45.7-52.1% out of sample (4 of 6). Scoring on PnL would not have produced a winner from that grid. Scoring on PnL is necessary once a candidate exists (blockers 1 and 2).
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed. trading_calibration.md:6 states the task as 'maximise accuracy at the expense of trading volume'. calibrate.py:135-140 scores on the Wilson lower bound or raw accuracy and drops zero-return trades. The clean P-A price-only rule had 56.1% accuracy but -226 gross and -658 net. The 5-min fade's average loss was 14.5 bps against an average win of 7.4. On the CSV, the top-2% 15-min fade wins 60.1% (n=268) but has avg win 18.9 against avg loss -21.1, so it nets -1.05. Caveats. Per-trade PnL is fat-tailed (std about 40 bps at H=15), so a PnL-gated search has less power than the accuracy gate, which makes blocker 2 worse. Also, pushing to the top 1-2% by |z| raised E|r| as a side effect, which partly helped with cost.
verdicts.notes: The accuracy objective came from the user's own earlier task wording, so changing it is the user's decision. The mechanism (negative-skew fades) is correct and is visible in the data.

verdicts.title: neural_trade's losses build in a short bias, and the decision layer turns it into a bet on market direction
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. Removing the bias removes a short-BTC beta, a confound that loses in rising markets. The unbiased head has AUC 0.487-0.513 (eval 7.1), and the research already re-centred it (dp = head - calibration median) without finding skill.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: I reproduced the focal-loss optimum numerically (alpha 0.7, gamma 1): 0.383 at P(up)=0.5. The head exceeds 0.5 only if P(up)>=0.70, exceeds 0.65 only if P(up)>=0.875, and falls below 0.35 once P(up)<=0.4376. trading_nocost.json: the 5-min median's up-share is below 0.5 in 12 of 12 runs, mean 0.278. But 4 runs are at 0.36-0.43, so 'biased' is accurate and 'always DOWN' is not. The 1-min and 15-min means are 0.509 and 0.485. The direction-head PnL equals -(always long) in exactly 18 of 36 cells. Clean, h=1: +763.9, t=2.04, in a -527.9 bps market. Notebook: 9 SHORT, 0 LONG, -$174 over 480 bars. Corrections. (a) Zero returns are masked, not labelled DOWN: mask = |ret| > deadband at model.py:1610-1612, and the metrics use the same mask (model.py:1947, 2051). (b) The alignment loss is negligible: weight 0.1 against lambda_dir clamped at 1000, under 1e-3 of the total (eval 3.2). (c) tau=0.4 (TAU_PRICE) applies to all three heads. Only the 5-min head is dominated by it, because lambda_point weights only h1 and clamps at 1000. The root cause is the zero-gradient trend term blowing up the loss-weight calibration (blocker 11).
verdicts.notes: This is a correctness fix that makes backtests interpretable and stops a deployed system from being short BTC by construction. It is not a profit source.

verdicts.title: The decision layer treats high predicted variance as risk to avoid, which inverts the cost logic (sizing, spike filter, stops)
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. With no direction edge, trading or skipping high-vol regimes gives the same expected gross (about 0). It matters only together with a direction signal, and then it is the same change as blocker 1.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: helper_functions.py is not imported anywhere in the repo (grep finds no import; eval 3.1 says so too). The 1.2x/0.6x sizing (lines 77-86) and the 2-6% stop (lines 61-75) are dead code, specified only in SRS FR-4.2/4.3 and 3.4.2. The notebook does apply conf=1/(1+v)>0.5 and a spike skip/exit (cell 5, lines 198, 269-293). But v is neural_trade's variance head, which ranks realised volatility at Spearman 0.05-0.16 frozen and -0.10 to 0.12 retrained daily, against 0.31-0.40 for EWMA (eval 7.9). So in practice these filters are close to random with respect to realised volatility, and the spike flag also uses a centred window (lines 196-197). a3.py reproduces: spike break-even 62.9%/59.0% vs no spike 71.3%/62.3%; low-vol tercile 85.7%/69.8% vs high-vol 64.1%/58.5%. The TP/SL levels (+0.5/+1.5/-1%) are reference only (lines 24-38).
verdicts.notes: The economic argument is right in principle (Kelly sizing on (mu-c)/sigma^2 is zero in quiet regimes). But it acts on code that is dead or fed by a variance head with almost no skill, so its current cost is small.

verdicts.title: Timestral-LIG was trained to have no direction, then judged on direction. Its variance objective is not weighted by decisions.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. A 1-3% sharper variance forecast barely moves a cost gate: free Parkinson EWMA already ranks |r| at Spearman 0.36-0.40, close to the ceiling that noisy |r| allows. The asymmetries cited are not stable.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: The LIG FAIL verdict rests on pre-registered QLIKE, pinball and tail rules against zero-shot (timestral_lig.md section 1, preregistration.json P1-P7), not on direction. Section 4.8 is labelled descriptive. The mathematics holds: symmetric averaging makes the variance even and the median odd. But the cited data effects do not replicate across horizons (a2.py). At H=5 the leverage coefficient has the opposite sign (+0.055*min(z,0)): realised/predicted variance is 3.76 after top-2% UP moves and 2.98 after DOWN moves. The 'even drift' term is -0.06|z| at H=5 against +0.36|z| at H=15, which is about 1 bps at |z|=3, far below cost. The proposed ablation already exists: symmetric averaging off (T-J; eval line 339) changed quality by -0.2% to +0.8%, with no QLIKE gain. The median random-walk penalty and the G shrink are confirmed (timestral_lig.md:139, 301; A1/A2 make no calls at 5 and 15 min).
verdicts.notes: Re-scoring on decision-relevant targets (Brier/AUC for |r|>c, ranking within the top volatility deciles) is cheap and sensible. It is not a hidden profit source.

verdicts.title: Labels and losses ignore costs: deadband 0, sub-cost noise dominates the labels, and an anti-shrinkage penalty
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. A cost-aware label cannot create information the inputs lack: a 6-feature walk-forward logistic reaches only AUC 0.517-0.541 (eval 7.6), and neural_trade sees only 60 close prices.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: DIR_DEADBAND_BPS=0.0 (model.py:119), and model.py has no fee, cost or PnL term. On the CSV, |r|<=4 bps for 62.8/33.7/19.8% of moves at 1/5/15 min, and <=10 bps for 91.3/66.3/45.0%. The vol_loss mechanism is refuted in practice. LAMBDA_VOL=1 is not calibrated while the other weights clamp at 1000, so it is under 1e-3 of the total (eval 3.2). Point forecasts are 2.5-17x smaller than real moves (eval 7.9), and the log shows val_vol_loss of 0.4-0.67 in scaled units, so forecast dispersion stays well below the realised level. The T-D evidence is selective. The neural_trade repo cells range from n=7 to 324 and from -4.7 to +8.4 bps per trade (e.g. 47 trades at +8.4, 254 at -1.6). The many 5-min trades come from the tau=0.4 short offset (about -0.25 sigma, about -2.4 bps), not from inflated dispersion.
verdicts.notes: A deadband or abstain class is a reasonable hygiene change. The 'anti-shrinkage penalty' part of the blocker is wrong as stated, because the term is inert.

verdicts.title: Monetisation routes that do not need direction are untested, and the data and scope restrictions rule them out
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No for an account at base fee tiers. Passive quoting on BTCUSDT is a latency and maker-rebate business, which needs VIP or market-maker fee tiers and colocation, not a better 1-min volatility forecast.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: It is true that these routes are untested, and SRS 10.3 confirms the scope: one pair and no execution module. The mechanism is mostly wrong. The BTCUSDT spot tick is 0.01 USDT (about 0.001 bps at about $110k), and the perp tick 0.1 is about 0.01 bps. The spread is usually one tick, so spread capture is about 0 against a 2 bps per side maker fee. The research's cost model (4 bps maker round trip with fills at the close) is optimistic, not pessimistic: a real taker round trip is about 10 bps. A cheap check on OHLC (scratchpad/obj/v_passive.py) puts passive entry for the top-2% 15-min fade at 0.5 or 1.0 sigma_1min, filled only if price trades through the limit. It fills 63% or 47% of signals, and gross per trade falls from +2.95 to +2.31 or +2.27 bps, which is adverse selection. On variance-risk-premium trades: the BTC option VRP exists without any forecast, and a 0.5-2.8% QLIKE gain at 1-15 min does not matter for options with days-to-weeks tenor and spreads of several vol points.
verdicts.notes: What remains valid is using the range forecast to time or size execution of trades decided on other grounds. That cuts costs but does not create alpha. A wider symbol universe (breadth) would help statistical power more than a quoting engine would.

verdicts.title: Model selection and stopping have no link to money, and the validation fold is also the test fold
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. Picking better among checkpoints that have no skill still gives a model with no skill. It matters for honest reporting only.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed in code. The checkpoint and restore_best_weights use val_loss (model.py:819-820). es_mcc has patience 15 against EPOCHS 8 (lines 45, 821-823), and es has patience = EPOCHS = 8, so neither fires. The 480-sample validation fold is also the test fold, and the notebook backtest runs on those same 480 bars (cell 5 output: 480 rows). Log: in rows 0-8, val_trend_loss is 4586.72 out of a val_loss of 4589.5-4590.3, which is 99.9%. In rows 13-44, val_dir_acc_h1 is 0.4948 with MCC 0. Corrections. In rows 0-12, accuracy is not uniformly 1.0: rows 2-5 and 10 show 0.598-0.971, all with MCC 0. The latest logged run (rows 61-65) is not dominated by the trend term: val_trend is about 0.001, and val_loss of 4.4-10.6 is mostly NLL. The log therefore mixes code versions.
verdicts.notes: This is a valid defect, and it shares a root cause with blocker 11 (the constant trend term).

verdicts.title: The notebook strategy's horizon, holding period and exits do not match the forecasts
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. The forecasts it would act on have no skill. Fixing it only makes the backtest honest.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed in inference.ipynb cell 5. max_hold is 30 (line 253). Entry and exit use only dir_5m (line 84). REV exits fire at <0.45 or >0.55 (lines 296-301), which means true P(up)<=0.62 for LONG and >=0.77 for SHORT under the focal optimum. weighted_sig uses config LAMBDA_* = 1/1/1 and drives no decision (lines 207-212). There are no fees (lines 310-315), and the windows are centred (lines 196-197). The cell with execution count 6 (index 7) prints 'Entry thresholds: 0.25 (buy) and 0.75 (sell)' (line 389) and draws them as horizontal lines (lines 253-254), while the code uses 0.65/0.35. Two more defects. check_multi_horizon_agreement(future_prices, 0) at line 266 tests only that 2 of 3 deltas share a sign, not that they agree with the trade side. And the whole backtest is 480 bars (8 h), the same fold that selected the weights.
verdicts.notes: The critic's low rating is correct.

verdicts.title: The trend and coherence prior points the wrong way for this market
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. Deleting the term removes the root cause of the loss-weight clamp, and through it the 5-min tau=0.4 short offset (blocker 4) and the constant val_loss (blocker 9). It adds no edge.
verdicts.corrected_evidence: model.py:1644-1676 is confirmed: the trend term compares true deltas with past pct_change*price, has zero gradient, and adds a coherence penalty. The critic understates its real harm, which comes from its size, not its direction. In raw USD^2 its median is about 1.2-1.7e5, so it dominates ref_loss, and lambda_point, lambda_dir and lambda_var all clamp at 1000 (model.py:783-800; eval 3.2). The reversal evidence on the CSV is weak. With non-overlapping origins, the OLS slope of the future return on z is -0.21 (t=-1.3) at H=5 and -0.39 (t=-0.8) at H=15. These are negative but not significant; the critic's -0.17/-0.39 come from overlapping origins. The 73-of-80 descriptive cells (trading_calibration.md 4.2) support the sign.
verdicts.notes: Delete the term, do not repair it. The 'anti-skill if repaired' risk is hypothetical. The clamp side effect is real and current.

blockers.title: LearnableIndicators do nothing in the forward pass, and the parameter logs hide it (D1/D7 go further than reported)
blockers.evidence: model.py:1073, 1085-1087, 1110-1112, 1135, 1147 compute logit + stop_gradient(logit)*(20-1), which equals 20*logit in the forward pass. I rebuilt the layer in numpy and ran it on the last 2,880 repo windows, scaled as in model.py:386-390. Forward alpha: 9.5e-7 at period 5, 9e-13 at period 9, 4e-30 at period 60. Of the 39 EMA-based channels, 34 are constant inside the window (within-window std < 1e-3): MA x3 and BB mid/upper/lower x9 equal the window's first bar, all 21 MACD/pair channels are 0, and RSI-21 and RSI-30 are 0. RSI-9 stays between 0 and 0.03 on a 0-100 scale (model.py:1138-1141), and one MACD-cross channel is float noise. The three BB %B channels equal (x - x0)/4e-4 + 0.5 (corr 1.0000 with x - x0, median |value| 347, range -3692 to +5397) and go unnormalised into the BiGRU (model.py:1239). The three momentum channels are identical at period 1.948 (D7). indicator_params_history.csv: all 27 EMA periods fall monotonically, and every logit rises by 0.00427 +/- 0.00002 per epoch whatever its type or period. That is one identical Adam step per variable, which points to a data-independent gradient: L2 decay toward logit 0 (REG_MOMENTUM_L2, model.py:67). The data gradient carries a factor sigmoid'(20*logit) of 1e-6 to 1e-30. ParamsLogger logs period_from_logit of the raw logit (model.py:1177-1194), so the CSV shows 'learned' periods of 4.9-58.8 while the forward pass uses periods of about 2e6 to 1e30. The tests check shapes only (test_model.py:392-426).
blockers.mechanism: The part of the architecture meant to supply the edge (data-adapted TA indicators) has never been tested. The network actually sees three things: the scaled level, a x2500-amplified (x - x0), and a ~2-bar momentum. The %B channels are 100-1000x larger than the other channels and saturate the GRU gates, so the recurrent layer sees roughly sign(x - x0). The 30 'learnable parameters' only decay. So nobody can know whether learnable indicators help.
blockers.fix_or_test: In the forward pass, use the logit itself. If a gradient boost is really wanted, use m*logit - stop_gradient((m-1)*logit). Under Adam the x20 gradient at model.py:1903-1905 only inflates the clip norm, so drop it. Replace the momentum write-back at model.py:1931 with the true inverse, raw = log(expm1(p-1)). Normalise each channel (LayerNorm) before the GRU. Add a unit test: forward alpha == 2/(period+1) at initialisation. Even after the fix, EMA-60 keeps 14% of its weight on the window's first bar after 59 steps (BB-50: 9%), and MACD 45/60/30 never warms up. So use a window of at least 3x the longest period, or seed the EMAs from a longer history. Decisive test: retrain with and without the fix, all else equal. Check that every channel varies inside the window and that the periods move apart. Then compare pinball and QLIKE on a held-out week.

blockers.title: The only measurable edge (volatility) is out of the model's reach: no range, volume or time-of-day inputs, and the one volatility channel is zeroed
blockers.evidence: The neural_trade variance head is 11-26% worse in QLIKE than a 2-parameter EWMA-Student-t. Its Spearman(width,|y|) is 0.03-0.16, against 0.31-0.40 for EWMA (plans/model_evaluation_timestral.md, table T-B, rows 'neural_trade as-is' and 'retrained daily'). The input is close only (model.py:1219). SRS 3.5.1 specifies 60-min OHLCV input, and SRS 3.2.2 lists 'price returns and volatility' and 'volume statistics' as fixed features; none of them is built. The only volatility-type channel, the BB std (model.py:1151-1153), is a constant 1e-4 under D1. There is no time-of-day input. On the repo CSV, mean |1-min return| varies 1.92x by UTC hour (3.23 bps at 23h, 6.20 bps at 14h), and the mean high-low range varies 2.17x. The variance output is a Student-t scale^2 in pooled-scaled units (model.py:1293, 1700-1733). It is centred on a price head pulled to q0.4 and clipped to 1e-4..1e4. The 60-bar context is far shorter than the 512-2048 bars behind Timestral's 0.5-2.8% QLIKE edge.
blockers.mechanism: Every monetisation route the research leaves open needs a sharp conditional-variance forecast: vol-scaled sizing, stop and target placement, trading only in high-vol regimes, quoting spreads, and options. High-low range, volume and the intraday seasonal pattern are among the strongest known predictors of next-minute variance. The model gets none of them, gets price levels instead of |returns|, and has its one volatility channel zeroed. So it loses to EWMA on the one quantity that is forecastable, and helper_functions' variance-based stops and sizing have nothing usable to consume.
blockers.fix_or_test: Build a variance-first variant. Inputs: log returns, |r|, Parkinson/Garman-Klass log(H/L), log volume, hour-of-day and minute-of-hour sin/cos, with a context of at least 512 bars. Output: log variance of returns per horizon, in unit-free return space. Loss: QLIKE or a Student-t NLL with zero location. Decisive test: on the repo holdout and the clean set, compare QLIKE with EWMA-t and HAR-RV (1/5/60/1440-min realised vol), with bootstrap CIs. Only if it beats EWMA-t, wire it into sizing and stops.

blockers.title: Training uses 0.06% of the available data and 40 optimizer steps, a cap written into the SRS
blockers.evidence: MAX_SEQUENCE_COUNT = 144*20 = 2,880 (model.py:48, applied at 348-356). SRS 3.2.1 and NFR-4.1 fix the same number. The logged notebook run (inference.ipynb cell 2 output) built 4,598,124 sequences (2017-01-01 to 2025-09-29) and kept 2,880 (0.063%). On the repo CSV the cap keeps 6.6% of 43,426. The last TimeSeriesSplit fold leaves 2,400 training samples, about 40 hours. BATCH_SIZE 576 (model.py:44) gives 5 batches per epoch, so 8 epochs = 40 Adam steps at lr 1e-3. No weight can move more than about 0.04 from its initial value, which matches the 0.004 per epoch drift of the indicator logits. By my count from model.py:1219-1320 the network has about 385k parameters (first MHA 132k, Flatten->Dense 92k, convs 51k, BiGRU 42k). That is 160 parameters per training sample, or about 2,400 per independent 15-min target (2,400/15 = 160 independent targets). The likely cause of the cap is compute: 33 sequential tf.scan EMAs per forward pass (math_helpers.py:249-253, parallel_iterations=1). The logged run took about 18 s per epoch for 2,880 samples (about 6.4 ms per sample), so the full 4.6M set would need about 8 h per epoch.
blockers.mechanism: After 40 steps on a single 40-hour regime, the model is essentially its initialisation plus a fit to that regime.
