Patterns that need many examples cannot be learned: conditional reversal after rare large moves, volatility regimes, time-of-day effects. The best val_dir_acc_h1 over 53 valid epochs is 0.522 on 480 overlapping samples, which is within noise.
blockers.fix_or_test: Replace the scan EMA with a causal convolution whose kernel is alpha*(1-alpha)^k over the window. That is one matmul and still differentiable in alpha. Drop the Flatten->Dense layer (24% of the parameters). Train on weeks to months with walk-forward folds and an early stop that can fire. Decisive test: a learning curve with 2 days, 1 week, 4 weeks and 6 months of training data, scored on a fixed later test window. If pinball and QLIKE improve with more data, the cap is binding. If the curve is flat, stop investing in this architecture.

blockers.title: The training objective cannot express 'no trade' and builds in a short bias
blockers.evidence: DIR_DEADBAND_BPS = 0 (model.py:119), so every minute is labelled UP or DOWN. On the repo CSV, 91% of 1-min, 66% of 5-min and 45% of 15-min moves are below 10 bps (mean |move| 4.2 / 9.6 / 16.5 bps). Two settings tilt toward DOWN: focal alpha = 0.7 on the DOWN class (model.py:113; math_helpers.py:130-134), and pinball tau = 0.4 on the 5-min price head (model.py:78, 1634). SRS 3.5.2 fixes alpha at 0.7. In training_log.csv, runs 4-10 (53 epochs with valid labels): the 5-min head predicted DOWN for every validation sample in 40 of 53 epochs and was never all-UP; the 1-min head did so in 29 of 53. In the notebook run the 5-min head called DOWN on all 480 samples (cell 3: TN 239, FN 241, F1 0), and the backtest made 9 trades, all SHORT (cell 5). The model has no cost term, no flat class and no output for expected return net of cost.
blockers.mechanism: Labels dominated by sub-cost moves teach the network to classify noise. The class weight and the q0.4 target then turn 'no information' into 'always short', so any backtest is a bet on the sign of the drift, not a test of the model. The only directional pattern found so far, reversal after large 5-15 min moves, lives in the 10-30% of minutes with large moves. Training on all minutes dilutes it 3-10x.
blockers.fix_or_test: Set FOCAL_ALPHA to 0.5 (or the empirical class ratio) and TAU_PRICE to 0.5. Set DIR_DEADBAND_BPS to the round-trip cost (8-10 bps). Then either use a 3-class up/flat/down head, or regress the expected return and trade only when |E[r]| > cost. Optionally add a differentiable PnL loss: position = tanh(f(x)), loss = -(position*r - c*|delta position|). Decisive test: on a held-out week, check that P(up) is centred on the base rate. Then measure the precision of calls with |E[r]| > cost and their net PnL after 4 and 10 bps, restricted to the large-move subset.

blockers.title: Price-level inputs and level-keyed layers bury the return signal (beyond the D8 drift)
blockers.evidence: The input is 60 raw closes, scaled per lag with a StandardScaler fitted on the training windows (model.py:386-390). On the last repo window the scaled input has std 1.69, the 1-min change has std 0.057 (3.4% of the input scale), and the mean within-window std is 0.15. meta_adjust (model.py:1223-1233) sets every indicator's logit offset from the window's mean and max price level. Flatten->Dense(32) (model.py:1278-1282, 92k parameters) maps each (time position x channel) value straight to the heads. The 1/5/15-min percent-change features are computed (model.py:246-279, listed as 'fixed features' in SRS 3.2.2) but are never model inputs. They feed only the zero-gradient trend loss (model.py:1644-1676).
blockers.mechanism: The network has to recover returns as tiny differences of large, drifting numbers, and two layers make the price level itself a feature. On 2,400 samples the easiest fit is 'price level of this 40-hour block -> delta', which breaks as soon as price leaves the block (D8: 88% of repo test origins were more than 3 sd out). The return features the code already computes go unused.
blockers.fix_or_test: Feed per-bar log returns, normalised by trailing volatility. Compute all indicators on returns or on price/last_close - 1. Drop the level-driven meta_adjust. Replace Flatten with pooling or a last-step readout. Pass extended_trends in as inputs. Decisive test: the same model with level inputs vs return inputs on the same split. Compare out-of-sample pinball and QLIKE, and the share of origins outside the training input range.

blockers.title: All training controls are no-ops, and the monitored metrics are degenerate or noise
blockers.evidence: EarlyStopping(val_loss, patience=EPOCHS=8) cannot fire within 8 epochs (model.py:47, 819). The advertised 'MCC early stopping' (model.py:86) monitors val_gauss_dir_mcc_h1 with patience 15 and restore_best_weights=False (model.py:821-826), so it never acts. ReduceLROnPlateau has factor 0.99 (model.py:828), so it cuts the LR by 1% at most. In runs 1-3 of training_log.csv, val_dir_acc_h1 = 1.000 is not skill: sensitivity is 0, specificity is 1, and val_gauss_dir_acc = 1.000 at all three horizons. Those validation sets therefore had no UP labels (a labelling bug in that code version), and every MCC was 0. Runs 4-7 are identical reruns (seed 42 at model.py:693; val_loss 4617.85, 4616.91, 4617.28 ... in each), so seed variance was never measured. CSVLogger(append=True) (model.py:818) mixes 10 runs from at least 3 code versions in one file. In run 2 (lambdas at 1) the zero-gradient trend term is 99.9% of the training loss: train loss goes 3013 -> 6695 -> 3469 -> 6871, tracking that term. In calibrated run 9 the term is 38-55% of the loss. So the epoch-loss plot in the notebook mostly shows batch-composition noise. Leakage check: I found no look-ahead in model.py. Windows end at t-1 and targets start at t, and the BiGRU and centred convs act only inside the past window. The only issues are a 14-sample train/val boundary overlap (no purge gap) and validation = test (D4).
blockers.mechanism: The developer cannot tell whether the model is learning, cannot stop or select on a meaningful signal, and could read 'accuracy 1.0' as success. Weight selection comes down to ModelCheckpoint on val_loss over the same 480 samples used for reporting, which inflates every reported number.
blockers.fix_or_test: Use separate train, validation and test sets with a purge gap of at least 15 bars. Monitor proper scores per horizon (pinball, QLIKE, direction log-loss) with the zero-gradient terms excluded. Set patience below the epoch count and restore the best weights. Remove the 0.99 scheduler. Assert that both classes are present in every validation set. Log the git hash and config with each run, and run at least 3 seeds.

blockers.title: Loss-weight calibration switches off regularisation and two point losses; one term rewards noisy forecasts
blockers.evidence: The logged calibration (inference.ipynb cell 2): med_ext = 48,295, which is the zero-gradient trend term, so ref_loss = 12,075. That clamps lambda_point, lambda_dir and lambda_var at 1000 and sets lambda_ext to 0.025 (model.py:785-804). All unscaled terms then shrink 1000x in relative weight: the L2 penalty (1e-4, added twice as reg_loss + inter_reg, model.py:1844-1845), the vol penalty (lambda 1, model.py:1775-1782) and the alignment term (0.1, model.py:1756). The 1-min and 15-min point losses keep weight 1 (model.py:1633-1635), so those price heads are set by the x1000 NLL alone. The vol penalty |std(pred_h1) - std(y_h1)| pushes forecast dispersion toward target dispersion. With correlation rho, such a forecast has MSE 2*sigma^2*(1-rho), about twice that of a constant forecast when rho is near 0. In runs 1-7 (lambdas at 1) it was the same order as the point loss (vol 0.0-0.5 vs point 0.7-1.0).
blockers.mechanism: A 385k-parameter model trains on 2,400 samples with effectively no regularisation. When calibration is off, it is rewarded for adding variance to forecasts that have no skill. Both raise out-of-sample error and produce spurious signals.
blockers.fix_or_test: Remove the trend term from the loss, or at least from the calibration. Scale each term by its own magnitude, or use uncertainty weighting. Move weight decay into the optimiser (AdamW). Delete the vol-matching penalty. Give each horizon its own point-loss weight. Test: the same seeds with and without these changes, comparing validation pinball and QLIKE and the dispersion of the price forecasts.

blockers.title: No consistent artifact for live inference: scalers, weights and the evaluated model come from different states
blockers.evidence: prepare_datasets refits and overwrites scaler_v3.joblib and scaler_v3_input.joblib on every call (model.py:379-393). With force=False, train_and_evaluate then loads the old weights and skips training (model.py:843-848). With force=True it warm-starts from the old checkpoint under the new scalers (model.py:850-854). ModelCheckpoint saves the epoch with the best val_loss (model.py:820). EarlyStopping restores weights only when it fires, which it cannot here (Keras 2, judging by the notebook's progress bar). So the reported metrics and backtest use the last epoch, while the file may hold a different one. Predictions exist only for the 480 X_test rows (model.py:872-899); no function scores the latest bar. Notebook cell 5 computes confidence = 1/(1+v), with v a Student-t scale^2 in pooled-scaled units. conf > 0.5 therefore blocks only when the predicted 5-min sd exceeds sqrt(3)*125 = 217 USD, about twice the typical 106 USD, so the gate rarely binds. The horizon weights come from Config.LAMBDA_SHORT/POINT/LONG (all 1). These are loss weights, not signal weights, and are not the calibrated lambdas.
blockers.mechanism: Even a model with skill would trade on inputs normalised by a scaler it was not trained with. The reported backtest may not describe the weights on disk, and the 'confidence' filter adds no protection.
blockers.fix_or_test: Save the weights, both scalers, the config and the lambdas as one versioned bundle (SRS NFR-2.3), and load all of it or nothing. Add predict_latest(df) that applies the saved scalers. Evaluate the checkpointed weights. Express confidence as predicted return sd in bps and gate on sd vs cost. Test: reload the bundle in a fresh process and reproduce the validation predictions exactly.

blockers.title: One target scaler across horizons tilts the Gaussian P(up) and lets the 15-min horizon dominate the shared trunk
blockers.evidence: model.py:379-383 fits one StandardScaler on the flattened 1/5/15-min deltas, and pred_mean/pred_scale are the same pooled values (model.py:712-713). The Gaussian P(up) and the alignment target test mu_scaled > 0 (model.py:1746-1754, 1969-1972, 2148-2151), but raw zero sits at -pred_mean/pred_scale. On the last repo window the pooled mean is +7.92 USD, against per-horizon means of 1.1 / 5.7 / 17.0 USD. The 1-min 'up' threshold therefore sits +0.17 sd above zero; over 29 two-day windows the median offset is 0.09 sd and the maximum 0.24 sd. That is a 4-9 pp tilt in P(up), with its sign set by the drift in the training window. The scaled target std is 0.38 / 0.85 / 1.46 for 1 / 5 / 15 min, so the 15-min pinball term is about 4x the 1-min term in the shared layers.
blockers.mechanism: The Gaussian direction signal, which the MCC monitor watches and the direction head is aligned to, carries a trend-following prior from the last 40 hours rather than a forecast. The shared trunk is fitted mostly to the 15-min horizon, which hurts the 1-min and 5-min towers.
blockers.fix_or_test: Use per-horizon scalers with the mean fixed at 0 (scale only), or train on unit-free returns divided by trailing volatility. Compute P(up) at the scaled image of raw zero. Test: reliability curves of the Gaussian P(up) before and after the change on a held-out week.

verdicts.title: LearnableIndicators do nothing in the forward pass, and the parameter logs hide it (D1/D7 go further than reported)
verdicts.corrected_evidence: I reproduced every number. Forward logit = logit + stop_gradient(logit)*19 = 20*logit (model.py:1073, 1085-1087, 1110-1112, 1135, 1147). meta_adjust is tanh*0.5 (model.py:957, 1233), only +/-0.5 against forward logits of -14 to -68, so it cannot help. I rebuilt the layer in numpy on the last 2,880 repo windows with the per-lag scaler. All three %B channels have median |value| 346.5, range -3692 to +5398, and corr 1.0000 with x - x0, for meta_adjust 0 or +0.5. With correct alphas %B stays in about -0.7..1.7. The 39-channel count (34 constant) checks out. indicator_params_history.csv: every one of the 27 EMA logits drifts by 0.00427 per epoch (std across variables 6e-6). That fits Adam steps on the L2 gradient alone. The implied forward periods are 1.4e6 to 3e29. The momentum write-back asinh((p-1)/2) (model.py:1928-1932) has a fixed point at p = 1.948, which matches the CSV. The tests check shapes only (test_model.py:397-428). One more point: the GRU kernel limit is sqrt(6/(43+192)) = 0.16, so a %B input of about 350 saturates every gate. Adam's maximum drift of about 0.04 over 40 steps cannot shrink that weight to the roughly 3e-4 it would need.
verdicts.notes: The evaluation report already lists the core defect as D1/D7 (plans/model_evaluation_timestral.md:149, 155). The new content is the channel-level effect: %B x2500 saturates the BiGRU, and ParamsLogger logs raw-logit periods. This matters most for the variance route, not for direction. With the BB std pinned at 1e-4 and the GRU seeing only sign(x - x0), the network cannot see the size of returns. That is a plausible part of why its variance head ranks volatility at Spearman 0.05-0.16, against 0.31-0.40 for EWMA. The critic says nobody can know whether learnable indicators help. The Timestral-LIG study largely answers that. It used a correct, causal indicator bank, and the MACD, RSI, momentum and EMA-distance gates fell to 0.49-0.57. It found no direction skill, and A1/A2 lost money even at zero cost (timestral_lig.md:13-58, 4.8).
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. A correct indicator bank inside a much stronger backbone (LIG) added no direction skill and lost money even at zero cost. Fixing D1 is a precondition for any valid test of neural_trade, and it may let the variance head close part of its 11-22% QLIKE gap to EWMA-t. At best that reproduces a free baseline (FHS/EWMA).

verdicts.title: The only measurable edge (volatility) is out of the model's reach: no range, volume or time-of-day inputs, and the one volatility channel is zeroed
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Two figures need correcting from the report. As-is: QLIKE is 11-22% worse than EWMA-t and Spearman is 0.05-0.16. Retrained daily: QLIKE is 7.5-28% worse and Spearman is -0.10 to 0.12 (model_evaluation_timestral.md:71-72, 396-398). The critic gives 11-26% and 0.03-0.16. Close-only input (model.py:1219) and the unbuilt SRS 3.2.2/3.5.1 features (returns, volatility, volume, OHLCV) are confirmed. On the repo CSV, mean |1-min r| by UTC hour runs from 3.23 bps (23h) to 6.20 bps (14h), a 1.92x ratio, and the high-low range varies 2.17x. Both confirmed. But hour-of-day means explain only 2.6% of the variance of |r| and 0.6% of r^2. An EWMA(0.94) of past |r| already has corr 0.42 with the next |r|, and an EWMA of the range 0.43. In LIG, the range plus clock features helped repo QLIKE by only 0.38% and went the other way on the clean set (n.s.). Context: at ctx 64, Timestral itself is 1.4-2.5% worse than EWMA-t on pinball (report 7.3), so the 60-bar window is a real limit.
verdicts.notes: The diagnosis that the head cannot see volatility is right. The money mechanism is overstated. A better variance forecast creates no PnL in the strategy this repo implements (directional spot/perp). Vol-scaled sizing of a zero-mean signal still has zero mean minus costs. Variance-based stops on a near-random walk do not create edge either; they only change the shape of the loss distribution. Variance accuracy pays only through an instrument that prices it: options against implied vol, maker quoting where spread width follows sigma, or as a regime filter for a conditional directional signal. None of these exists in the code or the SRS. The bar is also low and free: FHS/EWMA-t already capture most of the measurable gain, and Timestral adds only 0.5-2.8% QLIKE on top of it.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: Only together with a route that monetises variance (options vs implied vol, or maker quoting), and only if the forecast beats free FHS/EWMA and, for options, implied vol. Nothing here measures implied vol. On its own, a variance-first neural_trade at best matches a 2-parameter baseline.

verdicts.title: Training uses 0.06% of the available data and 40 optimizer steps, a cap written into the SRS
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed from notebook cell 2's output: 4,598,124 sequences cut to 2,880; 2,400 train and 480 test; 5 batches per epoch; 8 epochs at 18.6 s/epoch (the first epoch 60 s). The parameter count of about 385k checks out: BiGRU 41.9k, first MHA 132k, Flatten->Dense 92.2k, convs 51.2k. There are 33 sequential tf.scan EMAs (math_helpers.py:249-253). The repo CSV share is 2,880/43,426 = 6.6%. Corrections: 'essentially its initialisation' is overstated. The Glorot limit of the 92k Flatten->Dense (fan_in 2,880) is about 0.045, so an Adam drift of up to about 0.04 can move those weights by their full initial scale. SRS NFR-4.1 states a capacity ('support up to 2880'); the hard limit is in SRS 3.2.1. The SRS also says 40 epochs and batch 144, while the code uses 8 and 576 (model.py:44-45), so the code is even more restrictive than the spec. The mechanism holds up: a 40-hour training window contains only about 24 non-overlapping 15-min moves above 30 bps and about 55 5-min moves above 20 bps. That is far too few to learn a conditional reversal of a few bps.
verdicts.notes: The cap is real and binding for learning anything conditional. But foundation models trained on vast corpora (Chronos-2, TimesFM, Timestral) show no 1-15 min direction skill on these sets. So more data should mainly improve the variance head, toward EWMA quality, not create directional alpha. The proposed learning curve (2 days, 1 week, 4 weeks, 6 months on a fixed later test) is the right cheap decisive experiment, and it decides whether this architecture deserves more effort. The conv-kernel EMA is also needed for compute. At the current 6.5 ms per sample, the full set takes about 8 h per epoch.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. It is a precondition for learning any rare-event pattern. The only directional candidate (reversal after large moves) was not significant after correction even on multi-week data, and it loses after 4 bps in one of the two sets. Lifting the cap would at best surface that weak pattern or improve variance.

verdicts.title: The training objective cannot express 'no trade' and builds in a short bias
verdicts.corrected_evidence: The mechanism is stronger than stated; the counts are weaker. Counts from training_log.csv runs 4-10 (53 epochs): the 5-min head was all-DOWN (sensitivity 0, specificity 1) in 33 epochs, not 40 (34 with sensitivity 0). The 1-min head was all-DOWN in 22, not 29 (25 with sensitivity 0). The 5-min head was also nearly all-UP in 2 epochs (runs 8-9, epoch 1: sensitivity 0.971, specificity 0.021), so it flips; it is not purely short. TAU_PRICE = 0.4 goes into point_huber for all three price heads (model.py:1460). After calibration, only the 5-min one keeps a material weight (lambda_point = 1000). The upgrade: with focal alpha 0.7 and gamma 1, the loss-minimising constant P(up) at a 50/50 base rate is 0.383 (0.30 for gamma 0). The notebook's entry thresholds (cell 5: dir_prob < 0.35 short, > 0.65 long) sit 0.03 below and 0.27 above that no-information centre. So shorts are almost mechanical and longs almost impossible, which explains 9 of 9 trades SHORT (-$174, no fees). Move sizes on the repo CSV are confirmed: mean |log move| 4.21 / 9.57 / 16.49 bps; share below 10 bps 91.2% / 66.1% / 44.7%. DIR_DEADBAND_BPS = 0 (model.py:119) is confirmed. The deadband machinery already exists (model.py:1603-1616) and is only switched off.
verdicts.notes: This is already partly known as D3 (P(up) < 0.5 at every origin in 13 of 18 seed-horizon runs). It is the direct cause of what the backtest trades: the backtest measures the sign of the drift over 8 hours, not the model. Fixing alpha, tau and the deadband removes a hidden drift bet and adds a no-trade region, which stops losses. It does not create a signal. Cost-aware labels only concentrate learning on the large-move subset, where the one weak pattern lives.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. It turns an implicit short-drift bet into honest no-trading, which reduces losses. It could matter only together with a real conditional signal, such as reversal after large moves surviving correction, with maker-fee execution (4 bps or less round trip).

verdicts.title: Price-level inputs and level-keyed layers bury the return signal (beyond the D8 drift)
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Numbers confirmed on the last 2,880 repo windows: scaled input std 1.692, 1-min change std 0.0571, mean within-window std 0.150. extended_trends is used only in the zero-gradient trend loss (model.py:1646-1648) and is never a model input. Confirmed. Flatten->Dense(32) with 92k parameters is confirmed (model.py:1278-1282). Two corrections. (1) meta_adjust (model.py:1223-1233) adds at most +/-0.5 to forward logits of -14 to -68, so under D1 it has no effect today; it would only become level-keyed after D1 is fixed. (2) The D1 %B channels equal (x - x0)/4e-4 + 0.5, so the GRU already receives a within-window return. It is saturated to its sign, so the network does not see levels alone. The D8 drift figure (88% of repo origins more than 3 sd out) is from the report (model_evaluation_timestral.md:155), where it was already recorded.
verdicts.notes: The level framing is a real reason the variance head fails out of sample: inputs leave the training range, and retraining daily did not fix it. It is already the documented defect D8, and the report's fix list (step 2f) already prescribes return inputs. In the TSFM study, return inputs did not create direction skill either: Chronos-2 with return input has pinball loss 3-8% lower at 1 min, but no direction skill.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. Return-normalised inputs are needed for a stable variance forecast. Models that already use return inputs (Chronos-2) show no tradable direction skill. This matters only as part of the variance-route package.

verdicts.title: All training controls are no-ops, and the monitored metrics are degenerate or noise
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: EarlyStopping(val_loss, patience = EPOCHS = 8) cannot fire. The MCC stop has patience 15 and restore_best_weights=False (model.py:819-826). ReduceLROnPlateau has factor 0.99 (model.py:828). Runs 1-3: val_dir_acc_h1 = 1.0 with sensitivity 0, specificity 1 and val_gauss_dir_acc 1.0, so the validation sets had no UP labels. Runs 4-7 are bit-identical (seed 42 plus TF_DETERMINISTIC_OPS, model.py:693-694; epoch-0 val_loss 4617.85). In run 2 the zero-gradient trend term is 99.89-99.97% of the loss; in run 9 it is 38-55%. The best val_dir_acc_h1 over runs 4-10 is 0.522. One overstatement: 'ModelCheckpoint ... inflates every reported number'. The reported metrics and backtest come from the in-memory last-epoch model, not from the checkpoint. With 8 candidates the selection inflation is small. In the logged run 9 the last epoch was also the lowest val_loss (2397.14). The real problem is that validation equals test (D4) and the purge gap is missing (a 14-bar target overlap at the train/val boundary).
verdicts.notes: This is research hygiene. It explains why nobody noticed that nothing works. Without it, no later fix can be judged. It does not cost money directly.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. It is needed to measure whether any other fix helps. It cannot create edge.

verdicts.title: Loss-weight calibration switches off regularisation and two point losses; one term rewards noisy forecasts
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed from notebook cell 2: med_ext = 48,294.56 and ref_loss = 12,074.72. lambda point/dir/var are clamped at 1000 and ext is 0.025 (model.py:785-804). point_h0 and point_h2 use lambda_short/lambda_long = 1 (model.py:1633-1635). In runs 1-7, vol_loss is 0.005-0.51 against point_loss 0.63-1.04. The report already says that align, vol and L2 fall below 1e-3 of the total after calibration (model_evaluation_timestral.md:140, D2). The overfitting mechanism is overstated. Only the indicator logits, the shared Dense and the towers carry L2 at all (model.py:1281, 1287...); attention, conv and GRU never had any. Dropout 0.1 stays. With 40 Adam steps the model is limited by under-training more than by overfitting. The vol penalty's pull toward target dispersion never showed up in practice: the report finds point forecasts 2.5-17x smaller than real moves.
verdicts.notes: The zero-gradient trend term hijacking the calibration is the real defect (D2), and removing it is a one-line change. The vol-matching penalty is mis-specified for a no-skill regime and should be deleted. At its current weight it is irrelevant.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. These are loss-hygiene fixes with no plausible path to edge.

verdicts.title: No consistent artifact for live inference: scalers, weights and the evaluated model come from different states
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: prepare_datasets overwrites both scalers on every call (model.py:392-393, again at 864-868). force=False loads old weights and skips training (model.py:843-848). There is no function that scores the latest bar; the only entry points are train_and_evaluate and train_model. Corrections: the scalers are deterministic for the same CSV and cap, so a mismatch arises only when the data changes. That is exactly the live case, so the risk is real but not present in the logged evaluation. In logged run 9 the checkpoint and the evaluated weights coincide, because the last epoch had the lowest val_loss. The LAMBDA_* horizon weights feed only weighted_sig, which the entry and exit logic never reads. Entries use the 5-min dir_prob, conf, agreement and spike, so that sub-claim does not matter. The confidence gate rarely binds, which is plausible: the scaled 5-min target sd is 0.848, giving a typical Student-t scale^2 of about 0.24 and conf of about 0.8. Additional finding: check_multi_horizon_agreement uses thresh 0.67, and 2/3 = 0.667 < 0.67, so 'agreement' actually requires all three horizons to agree.
verdicts.notes: This is a deployment blocker, not a profitability blocker. It must be fixed before any live capital. It does not explain the absence of edge.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. It is necessary for safe live use of any model, but a consistent artifact of a no-skill model still loses after costs.

verdicts.title: One target scaler across horizons tilts the Gaussian P(up) and lets the 15-min horizon dominate the shared trunk
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Last-window numbers confirmed: pooled mean +7.92 USD; per-horizon means 1.11 / 5.66 / 17.00 USD; scaled sd 0.378 / 0.848 / 1.459; 1-min offset 0.167 sd. Over 29 two-day windows the median 1-min offset is 0.088 sd and the maximum 0.20 sd (not 0.24), a tilt of 3.5-8.0 pp. For the 5-min head, which is the one traded, the last-window offset is only 0.074 sd (about 3 pp). The Gaussian P(up) feeds only metrics and the alignment term (LAMBDA_DIR_ALIGN 0.1, below 1e-3 of the loss after calibration). Focal-loss labels use raw returns (model.py:1606-1616), so they are unaffected. The claim that the 15-min horizon dominates the trunk is refuted for the calibrated run. There lambda_point = 1000 multiplies only the 5-min pinball, and the x1000 Student-t NLL scales each horizon's error by its own predicted variance. The 3.7x pinball ratio applies only to uncalibrated runs (all lambdas 1).
verdicts.notes: The fix is cheap and correct (per-horizon scale-only scalers, or unit-free returns over trailing vol), but its effect on decisions is second-order next to focal alpha 0.7 and tau 0.4.
verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No. It removes a small drift-following prior from a diagnostic and from an auxiliary loss term; it has no path to edge.

blockers.title: Horizon grid is fixed at 1/5/15 minutes, where round-trip cost is 25-100% of the average move
blockers.evidence: model.py:58 HORIZON_STEPS=[1,5,15]; model.py:41 LOOKBACK=60 bars; all research inherits this (trading_nocost.py:21 HORIZONS, calibrate.py HS=(1,5,15)). On the repo CSV, non-overlapping h-minute log returns have mean |r| of 4.2/9.6/16.4/33.2/62.1/155 bps at h=1/5/15/60/240/1440 min. With wins and losses equal to mean |r|, the break-even accuracy is 97.5/70.9/62.2/56.0/53.2/51.3% at 4 bps round trip and -/-/-/80.1/66.1/56.4% at 20 bps (spot). The break-even correlation of forecast and outcome at 4 bps is 0.79/0.36/0.21/0.105/0.057/0.026. The best measured direction AUC is 0.54 (rho about 0.12), and the literature reports 51.9-53.8% accuracy at 1-15 min. Script: <scratch>/blk/q1.py
blockers.mechanism: Cost is fixed per trade, but the move a signal can capture grows with sqrt(h). The system only searches the horizons where even a strong signal cannot pay for costs. At 1 day, 51-52% accuracy (the level the literature reports at 15 min) would clear 4 bps. A 60-bar lookback also cannot form multi-hour or multi-day features, so the system cannot reach those horizons.
blockers.fix_or_test: Add horizons of 60, 240 and 1440 min and a lookback of days to weeks, using returns, not price levels. Data: Binance public klines 2017+ (data.binance.vision, reachable from here) for BTC and at least 5 other liquid pairs. The 4.6M-bar 2017-2025 file the notebook already loads also works. Minimum evidence before building: a walk-forward test over at least 3 years, fitted on past data only, of one pre-registered rule per horizon, with a net Sharpe 95% CI above 0 at 10 bps round trip, pooled over the pairs. Detecting Sharpe 1 on one asset at 80% power needs about 8 years, so a cross-section of pairs is required.

blockers.title: Test windows of 6 and 14 days cannot detect an edge smaller than the cost, and the system uses 0.06% of the history it already holds
blockers.evidence: Deployed rules in research/timestral_lig/results/calibration.json: 29-108 trades and 9-25 bps standard deviation per trade, so the minimum detectable gross edge (80% power) is 3.8-9.9 bps per trade against a 4 bps cost. A 60% hit rate on 50 trades has a Wilson 95% CI of [46, 72]%. Confirming a +2 bps/trade net edge at H=15 (sd 23.5 bps) needs about 1,100 trades: 11 days if every slot trades, but about 160 days at the roughly 7 trades/day of the top-2% fade. Meanwhile inference.ipynb (cell 2 output) loaded 4,598,198 bars from 2017-01-01 to 2025-09-29 and cut them to 2,880 (model.py:48 MAX_SEQUENCE_COUNT; SRS NFR-4.1 writes this limit into the spec). dw_ccxt.py:31 hard-codes a 30-day fetch. The selection split V2 is 3 days.
blockers.mechanism: Any edge that could realistically exist (a few bps per trade, selective) reads as 'not significant' on these windows. The same windows let selection noise look like 60-75% accuracy on calibration data. Without years of out-of-sample data, the research can neither reject nor confirm a money-making rule, and every 'no edge' verdict is underpowered for the selective rules.
blockers.fix_or_test: Before any further modelling, rebuild the harness on multi-year data (2019-2026, 1-min, data.binance.vision) with rolling monthly walk-forward refits and a 15-min purge. Do a power calculation for each hypothesis before testing, and require n large enough that the minimum detectable edge is below half the cost. Keep the last 3+ months sealed for one confirmatory run.

blockers.title: The one measured skill (variance) has no path to PnL in any simulator or in the code
blockers.evidence: All economic tests are 1-unit sign trades: trading_nocost.py:24-31, calibrate.py:112-126 and 199, bench/metrics2.py:126-132, and inference.ipynb cell 5 lines 310-315 (profit = 1 BTC x price change). Sizing (helper_functions.py:77-86) and stops (61-75) are imported nowhere. So the QLIKE gains (0.5-2.8% vs FHS; 5-17% vs a range EWMA) cannot show up as money in any test. Vol targeting of a base strategy, measured here: long BTC scaled by EWMA sigma to a 50% vol target, daily 2022-01 to 2026-10 (1,705 days), 2 bps per side on weight changes, gives Sharpe 0.32 against 0.25 for buy-and-hold. The difference of +0.07 has a block-bootstrap 95% CI of [-0.20, +0.32]. Script: q6.py in the same scratchpad folder.
blockers.mechanism: A variance forecast earns money only when it sizes a position that has a positive mean: an edge, beta drift, carry or a volatility premium. Every research test held size fixed at 1 unit and had no positive-mean base, so the skill had nothing to act on. Even with a base, a commodity EWMA gives an improvement that cannot be told apart from zero over 4.7 years. The model's 0.5-2.8% QLIKE gain over FHS would be a small part of that. The plan's step 4 pass rule (per-day PnL difference CI excludes 0 within 3 months, model_evaluation_timestral.md section 9) will almost certainly fail for a 0.5-2.8% QLIKE gain.
blockers.fix_or_test: First decide which premium the variance forecast is meant to time (options VRP, carry or a directional edge), then test the forecast only inside that strategy. Decisive cheap test: in a position-sized backtest on multi-year data, compare weights from FHS, EWMA and the model's sigma. Adopt the model only if the CI of the per-day PnL difference excludes 0. If no base strategy with a positive mean exists, stop investing in variance-model quality.

blockers.title: Options and volatility-premium route never built: the premium exists, but the system forecasts at horizons no option trades
blockers.evidence: Deribit DVOL (30-day implied vol, public API, reachable) against forward 30-day realized vol from Binance daily closes, 2022-01 to 2026-10, n=1,736 days: implied above realized on 69% of days, mean +6.8 vol points. By year: 2022 +12.3, 2023 +6.5, 2024 +7.0, 2025 +6.6, 2026 to date -0.05. In 58 non-overlapping 30-day blocks, 71% are positive and the worst is -40 points. corr(DVOL, forward RV30) = 0.47 against 0.23 for trailing RV30, so the market's implied vol already beats a naive historical forecast. The system forecasts only 1-15 min ahead (model.py:58) from 60 bars, while the shortest listed option expiries are daily. The SRS never mentions options. Script: q3.py in the same scratchpad folder.
blockers.mechanism: The only place a volatility skill is paid for directly is the variance risk premium, which option sellers earn. The system cannot reach it: wrong horizon, no implied-vol input, no options data and no hedging model. In 2026 the premium was about 0, so timing matters, and that is where a better forecast would pay.
blockers.fix_or_test: Minimum evidence before building: (a) a 1-day and 7-day variance forecast (HAR or FHS on 1-min RV over 2+ years) that beats bias-corrected Deribit implied vol of the same tenor on out-of-sample QLIKE; (b) a delta-hedged short-straddle or variance-swap-proxy backtest with real bid/ask, Deribit fees and crash days included, in which the forecast-timed version beats always-short with a CI excluding 0. Data: Deribit option quote history (Tardis.dev or Deribit history), DVOL (free), 1-min perp for hedging.

blockers.title: Rules were selected on accuracy with scale-free confidence, and a volatility-regime gate was never tested
blockers.evidence: calibrate.py:135-141 scores rules by the Wilson lower bound or raw accuracy, not net PnL. All confidence measures are divided by sigma (z = median/IQR, P(up)-0.5, price z = r_H/(sigma*sqrt(H)); calibrate.py:78-101), so no rule depends on the absolute volatility level. At H=15, by causal EWMA-sigma tercile: mean |r15| = 10.1/15.5/23.8 bps, break-even accuracy at 4 bps = 69.9/62.9/58.4% (56.1% in the top decile), and at 10 bps = 99.6/82.2/71.0%. Mean |1-min return| is 3.23 bps at 23 UTC and 6.20 bps at 14 UTC. The only rule that made money net (the top-2% fade) did so on the higher-volatility repo window (mean |r1| 5.0 bps) and lost on the quieter clean window (3.0 bps), where average losses were 14.5 bps against average wins of 7.4 bps (trading_calibration.md section 5). Script: q2.py.
blockers.mechanism: With cost fixed in bps, profit depends on accuracy times the size of the move. Scale-free filters take low-volatility trades, where costs eat the whole move, as readily as high-volatility ones. An accuracy objective also ignores asymmetric payoffs. This is the cheapest way for the variance forecast to enter the directional strategy, and nobody has tried it.
blockers.fix_or_test: Rerun the existing calibration with two extra rule dimensions, a causal sigma-level gate (tercile or decile of the forecast sigma) and an hour-of-day gate, and an objective of the Wilson lower bound of mean net PnL at 4 bps. Keep the circular-shift selection gate. Minimum evidence: on at least 3 months of new data with at least 300 trades, high-sigma-regime accuracy at or above the regime's break-even accuracy (about 58%) and net PnL CI above 0.

blockers.title: The trade simulator charges a full round trip on every trade, assumes free fills at the close, and cannot net positions
blockers.evidence: Cost is subtracted per trade: calibrate.py:199 (pnl - c), metrics2.py:132, and fills happen at the forecast bar's close with no delay. For always-in signals, 48-51% of consecutive trades are on the same side, so accounting on position changes charges 2.06 bps/trade instead of 4.00. That moves break-even accuracy from 62.2% to about 56.3% at H=15 and from 56.0% to 53.0% at H=60. Selective rules are unaffected (3.8-4.0). In the other direction, the 4 bps (maker) assumption is optimistic. A passive bid at close minus k*sigma (k=0.5-3), filled only on a trade-through, fills 1.3-42% of minutes and is 1.1-1.5 bps under water at the fill bar's close before fees, so a maker fill is not free. The taker round trip is 10 bps. There is no paper or live loop to measure real costs (SRS 9.3 and 10.3: no order execution, no streaming). Script: q4.py.
blockers.mechanism: The cost model decides every verdict, yet it is a guess. It overstates costs for persistent signals and for the standard weak-signal design (aim position, no-trade band, partial rebalancing). It understates costs for anything that assumes maker fills. Slow signals could be wrongly rejected, and fast ones wrongly accepted.
blockers.fix_or_test: Replace the 1-unit sequential simulator with a position-based backtester. Charge cost per unit of turnover, with taker and maker modes, model passive fills as trade-through plus markout, include a no-trade band, and allow overlapping staggered positions of size 1/H. Rerun T-D and the calibration on it. Before any capital, run a paper-trading loop on the exchange testnet or live books for 2-4 weeks to measure actual fees, slippage and latency against the assumed 4/10 bps.

blockers.title: Single symbol, single venue, close-only input: the extra information outside spot closes is never read
blockers.evidence: dw_ccxt.py:48-49 fetches only BTC/USDT spot 1-min bars. model.py:244 returns only the Close column, dropping high, low and volume. Timestral-LIG found that 51 of 62 close-derived features added nothing; only non-close inputs (range, clock) helped (timestral_lig.md section 5). Measured here on the repo window with Binance perp 1-min klines: lagged return correlations between perp and spot are -0.007 to -0.02 (no lead-lag at 1 min). The perp-spot basis minus its 60-min mean predicts the next 1-min spot return with corr +0.041 (n of about 43.5k) and the next 5-min return with +0.036. That beats every model's direction skill, but it is worth only about 0.2 bps per 1-min trade against 4 bps cost. It is one in-sample 30-day window, and one of about 10 correlations computed. Script: q6.py.
blockers.mechanism: A martingale close series has nothing to learn, so any directional information must come from other series: perp, basis, order flow, other venues, other assets. The pipeline can only see one spot close series, so it cannot find that information even if it exists. At taker cost the measured basis signal is too small to trade alone. It is useful as a skew input for passive execution.
blockers.fix_or_test: Ingest BTCUSDT perp klines, aggTrades and funding (free, data.binance.vision), ETH, and a second venue. Minimum evidence: walk-forward over at least 3 months of new data in which cross-venue and flow features reach AUC of at least 0.55 at 5-15 min and maker-cost PnL with a CI above 0. Otherwise use the features only to time execution.

blockers.title: Funding and basis carry never evaluated: it is the only route measured positive here, but its return above cash is small
blockers.evidence: Binance BTCUSDT perp funding, 2022-01 to 2026-09 (5,202 prints, data.binance.vision): mean 0.60 bps per 8 h, or 6.6%/yr gross for long spot / short perp. By year: 4.2/7.9/12.0/5.1% and 2.9% annualized in 2026 to date. 53 of 57 months were positive (2026-02 to 04 negative). AR(1) is 0.77. Switching on the trailing 7-day mean does not help after 30 bps per on/off cycle: 4.9%/yr (threshold 0) and 0.8%/yr (threshold 0.5 bps). The downloader and SRS have no perp, funding or margin data. Script: q5.py.
blockers.mechanism: This is a market-neutral premium that needs no forecast, and the system's spot-only, directional scope rules it out. The measured excess over a cash yield is roughly 0-3%/yr, it needs capital on both legs, and the short perp carries liquidation risk. It sets a minimum hurdle for any capital-using strategy rather than offering a large opportunity.
blockers.fix_or_test: A 1-day study: a carry backtest net of 4-leg fees, margin buffer and a USD cash-rate opportunity cost over 2019-2026. Build it only if net excess Sharpe is at least 1 with a CI above 0. Use the variance forecast only to size the margin buffer.

blockers.title: Market making with volatility-adaptive quotes cannot be built on 1-min spot OHLCV at a retail fee tier
blockers.evidence: No L2 book, trade or websocket data (dw_ccxt.py:65 uses only fetch_ohlcv; SRS 10.3 states 'No Real-time Data Streaming'). The bar-level test in q4.py: trade-through fills of a bid at close minus k*sigma (k=0.5, 1, 2, 3) have markout of -1.25/-1.13/-1.28/-1.53 bps at the fill bar's close and -2.41/-1.80/-0.99/-3.40 bps at 60 min, before a 2 bps per side maker fee. blockers.fix_or_test: Pursue this only if a maker-rebate or VIP fee tier is available. Minimum evidence: a queue-aware simulation on tick and L2 data (Binance futures bookTicker and aggTrades, or Tardis) for a pair whose quoted spread exceeds 2x the maker fee, showing positive 1-10 s markout after fees and that sigma-adaptive width beats constant width. Otherwise drop this route.

blockers.title: SRS exit and sizing layer (three-tier TP, variance stops, confidence sizing, risk limits) is unwired or mis-scaled, and cannot create money without an edge
blockers.evidence: inference.ipynb cell 5 lines 24-38: TP +0.5%/+1.5% and SL -1% are 'not executed, just reference'. Within the 30-bar max hold (line 253), +0.5% is touched in 10.9% of entries, +1.5% in 0.53% and -1% in 1.95%. The SRS stop of 2% x (1+ratio), i.e. 2-6% (helper_functions.py:61-75), is touched in 0.13% (2%) and 0.000% (4% and above) of 30-bar windows. FR-4.2/4.3/4.4 and FR-5.3, Backtrader, the predict API (SRS 6.5) and live execution (9.3) are not implemented. Script: q2.py.
blockers.mechanism: With a near-martingale price (lag-1 autocorrelation -0.011), stops, targets and scale-outs have zero expected gross PnL (optional stopping) and only add turnover and cost. Building these SRS items as specified will not make money. The fixed-percentage levels are also 4-60 standard deviations of the holding-period move, so they would never trigger. Risk limits matter only for survival once an edge exists.
blockers.fix_or_test: Defer Backtrader, the API and live execution until a pre-registered edge passes on multi-year data. Then replace fixed-percentage levels with sigma-scaled quantile exits (as risk control, not as a profit source) and add exposure, leverage and drawdown limits. verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: Only in combination. A longer horizon creates no edge by itself. It moves the cost bar to where known premia (trend, carry) exceed costs. Daily trend rules show positive but non-significant net Sharpe over 4.8 years, so profit needs one pre-registered rule tested on multi-year, multi-asset data. The neural model is not needed for that route.

verdicts.title: Test windows of 6 and 14 days cannot detect an edge smaller than the cost, and the system uses 0.06% of the history it already holds
verdicts.corrected_evidence: Confirmed: the deployed rules have 29-107 trades, and the sd per trade implied by mean/t in research/timestral_lig/results/calibration.json is about 9-21 bps, so the minimum detectable edge is 3.8-9.9 bps. The Wilson CI for 60% on 50 trades is [46.2, 72.4]. A +2 bps edge at sd 23.5 needs about 1,082 trades. inference.ipynb cell 2 output shows 4,598,198 bars (2017-01-01 to 2025-09-29) cut to 2,880 sequences (0.063%). SRS.md:473 NFR-4.1 writes this limit into the spec, dw_ccxt.py:31 fetches 30 days, and V2 is 3 days (timestral_lig.md section 3). Overstated: dense signals are NOT underpowered. At H=1 over 6 days the minimum detectable edge is 0.19 bps. A2 made 2,558 trades at -0.235 bps each (t -1.62). My dense-fade check gives gross -0.02±0.89 (repo, H=15), +0.39±0.58 (clean, H=15), and +0.07±0.30 / +0.01±0.19 (H=5). Together these rule out even a 1-2 bps gross edge for always-in signals. verdicts.would_fixing_it_plausibly_create_profit: No, not on its own. More data only shows whether an edge exists. It is a prerequisite for confirming any selective or long-horizon rule (blockers 1, 4 and 8), so it is needed in combination with any of them.

verdicts.title: The one measured skill (variance) has no path to PnL in any simulator or in the code

Every simulator trades 1 unit on the forecast sign: trading_nocost.py:24-31, metrics2.py nonoverlap_trades (about lines 126-136), calibrate.py:199, and inference.ipynb cell 5 lines 310-315. q6 reproduces: vol-managed Sharpe 0.32 against 0.25 for buy-and-hold, difference +0.07, CI [-0.20, +0.32]. Correction: variance does enter the notebook strategy, but only as a filter, never as sizing. confidence = 1/(1+var) must exceed 0.5, and a spike gate uses var_mean = np.convolve(mode='same'), a centred mean that looks ahead (cell 5 lines 174-197 and 269-293). Also, the measured QLIKE gains are at 1-15 min, while vol targeting and VRP need forecasts at 1-30 days, so the existing skill would not transfer even if wired.

Even a plain EWMA vol target over 4.7 years adds a non-significant +0.07 Sharpe. It helps only together with a base premium (trend, carry, VRP) and a forecast at that base's horizon.

verdicts.title: Options and volatility-premium route never built: the premium exists, but the system forecasts at horizons no option trades

Overstated: (a) As a variance-swap payoff, (IV^2-RV^2)/(2*IV) per 30-day block, the premium is +3.5 to +5.1 vol points (3 block offsets, n=57 each), with annualized Sharpe 0.77-1.13 before any option costs. In-sample pre-cost Sharpe is about 0.8-1.1, with crash blocks of -55 to -74 vol points and a negative 2026. It needs Deribit quote history, fees, spreads, delta hedging and tail sizing.
